author: copilot
body:
Branches with unresolved conflict markers were repeatedly merging into `master` because nothing in the pipeline blocked them. Root causes: no CI check for conflict markers, a completely broken `cleanup-conflicts.js` (corrupted regex + always-false guard), and `auto-merge-to-master.yml` attempted the merge with no pre-flight validation.

## Changes

### New: `scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.js`
Scans source files (`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.css`, `.json`) for real conflict marker lines using precise start-of-line patterns:
```
/^<{7}\s/   <<<<<<< HEAD / branch-name
/^={7}\s*$/ =======
/^>{7}\s/   >>>>>>> branch-name
```
Exits non-zero and reports offending file + line numbers. Correctly ignores markers inside `.md` code fences and string literals.

### Fixed: `scripts/cleanup-conflicts.js`
- Guard was `!txt.includes('')` (always `false`) — fixed to check for `'<<<<<<<'`
- Replacement was a truncated comment with no actual code — replaced with a working multiline regex that strips conflict blocks keeping the HEAD/ours side
- Added Windows CRLF round-trip preservation; excluded `.md` files

### CI: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
Added `check-conflicts` job (runs `check-no-conflict-markers.js`) that the existing `verify` job now `needs`. Conflict-laden branches fail CI before any build work begins.

### Auto-merge gate: `.github/workflows/auto-merge-to-master.yml`
Checkout + conflict marker check added as steps **before** the merge API call. Branches with unresolved markers fail the workflow instead of being merged.

### Local gate: `.githooks/pre-push`
Calls `check-no-conflict-markers.js` and blocks the push if markers are found, catching the issue before it ever reaches CI.

### `package.json`
`check-conflicts` script added; prepended to `smoke` so `npm run verify` also catches conflicts locally.

author: via-decide
body:
## Why everything was broken

**6 standalone HTML files** at the repo root (`discover.html`, `about.html`, `profile.html`, `games.html`, `agent.html`, `auth.html`) were intercepting every navigation. When you tapped Discover, Vercel served `discover.html` (a separate old page with CREATOR FLOW / SURFACE layout) instead of the main app.

PR #193/194 also added a **Vite build** (`shell/index.html` → `dist/`) that further broke Vercel deployment.

## What this fixes

### 1. Moved 6 hijacking files → `_legacy-pages/`
No longer at root, so `/discover` no longer serves `discover.html`.

### 2. Deleted Vite build system
- Removed `vite.config.js`, `shell/index.html`
- Cleaned `package.json` (no more build/dev/preview scripts)
- This is a static site. Always was.

### 3. Rewrote `vercel.json` from scratch
- `framework: null`, `buildCommand: null` — just serve files
- `cleanUrls: false` — prevents .html file interception
- 11 explicit rewrites: `/tools`, `/discover`, `/about`, `/profile`, `/games`, `/explore`, `/feed`, `/agent`, `/auth`, `/deepdives` → all serve `index.html`

### 4. URL-based layer switching
When `index.html` loads at `/tools`, it reads the URL and calls `switchLayer("tools")` automatically. Works on both Vercel and GitHub Pages.

## After merge
- `viadecide.com/tools` → Tools grid with 68 tools
- `viadecide.com/discover` → Discover layer (the real one)
- `viadecide.com/about` → About layer
- `viadecide.com/games` → Tools grid filtered to Games
- All tabs/buttons work without leaving the main app

author: atoxic374-alt
body:
### Motivation
- Interaction `customId` parsing assumed fixed underscore-separated token indexes, which breaks when `panelId` contains underscores and causes claims, logging, and point actions to resolve the wrong channel/panel.
- The goal is to robustly extract `guildId`, `panelId`, and `channelId` from a `customId` so ticket actions work correctly for panel IDs with underscores.

### Description
- Added a reusable helper `parseTicketGuildPanelChannel(customId, guildIndex)` that takes the guild token index, uses the last token as `channelId`, and joins middle tokens into `panelId` (defaulting to `'default'`).
- Replaced many brittle `parts = id.split('_')` + hardcoded index lookups for button/select/modal handlers with the new parser for actions including `claim`, `close`, `reassign`, `delete`, post-close point controls, `transfer`, `rename`, `add`, `remove`, `ping`, and the open button/menu handlers.
- Updated modal handlers (`ticket_rename_modal_*`, `ticket_add_modal_*`, `ticket_remove_modal_*`) to use the same parser so modals also work when `panelId` contains underscores.
- Changes are localized inside `commands/ticket.js` and aim to preserve existing semantics while fixing incorrect token alignment for multi-part panel IDs.

### Testing
- Performed a syntax/parse check with `node --check commands/ticket.js`, which completed successfully.
- Verified the modified file `commands/ticket.js` passes Node's static parse validation with no syntax errors.

body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a complete feedback analysis dashboard that integrates with ChannelTalk to collect customer feedback and uses Claude AI to automatically categorize and visualize the results.

## Key Changes

### Core Features
- **Feedback Collection**: Integrated ChannelTalk API to fetch FeedbackBot messages within a specified date range
- **AI Categorization**: Implemented Claude Sonnet 4 integration to automatically categorize feedbacks into 3-10 thematic groups
- **Interactive Dashboard**: Built a React-based UI with date range picker, category visualization, and filterable feedback list

### Components
- `app/page.tsx`: Main dashboard page with state management for fetching, analyzing, and displaying results
- `components/DateRangePicker.tsx`: Date range input with preset defaults (last 30 days)
- `components/CategoryChart.tsx`: Bar chart visualization of feedback distribution across categories with interactive selection
- `components/FeedbackList.tsx`: Scrollable list of feedbacks with filtering by category, displaying title, user voice, manager comments, and metadata

### Backend APIs
- `app/api/feedbacks/route.ts`: GET endpoint that fetches feedbacks from ChannelTalk API using date range parameters
- `app/api/analyze/route.ts`: POST endpoint that sends feedbacks to Claude for categorization

### Utilities
- `lib/channeltalk.ts`: ChannelTalk API client with message parsing logic to extract feedback structure (title, user voice, manager comment, channel, plan, author)
- `lib/claude.ts`: Claude API integration for feedback analysis with JSON response parsing

### UI/UX
- Summary cards showing total feedbacks, category count, and most common category
- Color-coded category chips with feedback counts
- Loading states with spinner animation
- Error handling with user-friendly messages
- Responsive design with Tailwind CSS

## Implementation Details
- Uses Next.js 16 with App Router and server components
- Implements multi-step async workflow: fetch → analyze → display
- Parses FeedbackBot message format using regex patterns to extract structured data
- Claude prompt engineered to generate consistent JSON output with category names, summaries, and feedback ID mappings
- Interactive filtering allows users to click chart bars or category chips to view specific category feedbacks

author: sigilante
body:
## Summary

Fixes the 4 failing kernel-boot integration tests.

### Root Causes

1. **QEMU raspi4b requires `-m 2G`** — without it, `PILL_BASE` (0x10000000 = 256MB) is inaccessible. Added to all QEMU invocations in `Makefile`, `tests/kernel-boot.sh`, and `tests/run_tests.sh`.

2. **`KERNEL` must be typed explicitly** — `cold_start` points to `word_quit`, not `word_kernel`. Updated `boot_pill()` and `boot_pill_event42()` helpers to send `KERNEL\n` after boot.

3. **`set -e` + `[[ VERBOSE ]] && cmd`** — when `VERBOSE=0`, the `&&` short-circuits with exit code 1, aborting the script after the first test. Fixed with `|| true`.

4. **`pill_load`** reverted to simple `qnbytes > 0` check — the magic sentinel approach crashed when accessing `PILL_BASE` through a C function (QEMU raspi4b memory quirk).

### Result

```
5/5 passed
```

All 376 REPL tests continue to pass.

## Summary

Implements method combinations (before/after daemons) inspired by LFE Flavors and CLOS, as specified in ADR 0005 and ADR 0006.

- Adds `before_methods` and `after_methods` maps to the class state record in `beamtalk_object_class.erl`
- Implements registration API: `add_before/3`, `add_after/3`, `remove_before/2`, `remove_after/2`, `get_before_methods/2`, `get_after_methods/2`
- Integrates method combinations into `beamtalk_dispatch.erl` with ADR 0006 ordering: before methods run superclass->subclass, after methods run subclass->superclass
- Before methods can short-circuit (skip primary method and return early)
- After methods receive and can transform the primary method's result
- Zero overhead fast path when no daemons are registered
- Error resilience: daemon crashes are caught and logged, dispatch continues
- Depth guard on chain walk matching `MAX_HIERARCHY_DEPTH`

## Key Changes

- `runtime/apps/beamtalk_runtime/src/beamtalk_object_class.erl` — class state + registration handle_call clauses
- `runtime/apps/beamtalk_runtime/src/beamtalk_dispatch.erl` — `invoke_with_combinations`, collection, execution
- `runtime/apps/beamtalk_runtime/test/beamtalk_method_combinations_tests.erl` — 16 EUnit tests

## Test Plan

- [x] Registration: add/get/remove before and after daemons
- [x] Multiple daemons on same selector (order preserved)
- [x] Dispatch fast path with no daemons
- [x] Before method short-circuit skips primary
- [x] After method transforms result
- [x] Hierarchy ordering: before=superclass->subclass, after=subclass->superclass
- [x] Error resilience: crashing daemons don't break dispatch
- [x] Collection on unknown class returns empty
- [x] Full CI passes (clippy, fmt, dialyzer, all tests, e2e)

body:
import asyncio
import random
import sys

class Universe:
    def __init__(self, id):
        self.id = id
        self.entropy = 0
        self.is_alive = True
        self.constants = {
            "gravity": random.uniform(6.6, 9.8),
            "light_speed": random.randint(200000, 300000),
            "life_probability": random.random()
        }

    async def evolve(self):
        while self.is_alive:
            self.entropy += random.random()
            if self.entropy > 100:
                print(f"🌌 Vũ trụ #{self.id} đã đạt mức nhiệt chết. Đang tái cấu trúc...")
                self.is_alive = False
            await asyncio.sleep(0.1)

async def big_bang():
    print("⚡ Đang khởi động Giao thức Khai sinh... 3.. 2.. 1..")
    universe_count = 0
    
    while True:
        universe_count += 1
        new_universe = Universe(universe_count)
        print(f"✨ Một vũ trụ mới vừa ra đời: ID-{new_universe.id} | G={new_universe.constants['gravity']:.2f}")
        
        # Chạy tiến hóa đa vũ trụ song song
        asyncio.create_task(new_universe.evolve())
        
        await asyncio.sleep(0.5)
        if universe_count > 10: # Giới hạn để máy bạn không biến thành hố đen
            print("\n⚠️ CẢNH BÁO: Đa vũ trụ quá tải! Đang đóng cổng không gian...")
            break

if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        asyncio.run(big_bang())
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print("\n🛑 Bạn đã dừng dòng chảy thời gian.")

## What is it?

`bore` is a minimal TCP tunnel written in Rust (~400 lines) that exposes
local ports to a remote server, bypassing NAT firewalls. It is similar to
ngrok and localtunnel but focused purely on TCP forwarding — no frills,
easy to self-host, with optional HMAC-based secret authentication.

<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

Implement a **Public Meter** system for `georgi-cole/bbmobilenew`.

## Goals
Add a new public sentiment gameplay module that tracks audience approval for players throughout the season, updates every cycle based on gameplay and social behavior, is accessible from the existing FAB entry named **`Public Meter`**, and introduces **The Public’s Jury Vote** in the finale.

## Product requirements
### Public approval system
- Track public approval for **all players** on a `0–100` scale.
- Initialize approval with a configurable default (recommended `50`).
- Approval should update **each cycle** based on a combination of:
  - competition performance,
  - strategic actions,
  - nomination / eviction behavior,
  - social interactions from the social module,
  - public-request completion or failure.
- Approval updates should be deterministic, configurable, and clamped to valid ranges.
- Persist prior-cycle approval so UI can show trend changes.

### Public directions / requests
- Add a system for audience-driven requests/objectives, such as:
  - getting closer to a player,
  - targeting or protecting a player,
  - winning a competition,
  - making a bold move,
  - apologizing, exposing, aligning, confronting, etc.
- Requests should be derived from current game context and social dynamics.
- Each request should support statuses such as active / completed / failed / expired.
- Completing requests should increase approval; failing or acting against them should reduce approval.
- Requests should be feasible, varied, and configurable.

### FAB integration
- Reuse the existing FAB entry/hook labeled exactly **`Public Meter`**.
- Do **not** add a duplicate navigation entry for this feature.
- Opening the FAB item should show the Public Meter experience.

### Public Meter UI
Implement the Public Meter interface exposed from the FAB hook with sections for:
- **Your Approval**
  - approval bar,
  - exact percentage,
  - trend since previous cycle,
  - descriptive label/band.
- **Public Rankings**
  - all players ranked by approval,
  - approval values or chosen visibility representation,
  - trend indicators.
- **Public Feed**
  - recent audience sentiment updates explaining approval changes.
- **Public Requests**
  - active and resolved requests with outcomes.

### Finale integration: The Public’s Jury Vote
Introduce a finale change where **The Public is one additional final jury voter**.

Rules:
- The Public vote must consider **only the finalists**.
- Eliminated players are **never eligible** for the Public’s Jury Vote, even if they had higher public approval than the finalists.
- At finale, compare final public approval **between the finalists only**.
- The finalist with the higher approval receives **1 Public jury vote**.

Example rule that must be preserved:
- If finalists are X and Y, and eliminated players A and B have much higher public approval, the Public still chooses **only between X and Y**.

### Tie-breakers for the Public’s Jury Vote
If finalists tie in public approval, resolve deterministically in this order:
1. higher season-average approval,
2. more completed public requests,
3. higher final-cycle approval,
4. higher cumulative positive approval delta across the season.

## Technical expectations
- Implement the system in a way that fits the repo’s current TypeScript-heavy architecture.
- Prefer a config-driven / event-driven design over scattering hardcoded approval logic.
- Hook into existing cycle-resolution and social-module flows where appropriate.
- Keep balancing values configurable.
- Add or update tests for public approval calculation, request resolution, finale vote eligibility, and tie-break behavior.

## Suggested architecture direction
Create/extend modules along these lines as appropriate for the existing codebase:
- `PublicOpinionService` for approval state and cycle updates
- `PublicDirectionService` for request generation/evaluation
- `PublicFinalVoteService` for finalist-only Public jury vote resolution
- config definitions for weights, caps, labels, and tie-break rules

## Acceptance criteria
- A working Public Meter experience is reachable from the existing FAB item named **`Public Meter`**.
- Approval is tracked for all players and updates each cycle.
- Public requests are generated and resolved with visible outcomes.
- The UI explains approval, trends, rankings, feed updates, and request state.
- The finale includes **The Public’s Jury Vote** as one extra vote.
- The Public vote considers **only finalists**.
- Deterministic tie-breakers are implemented exactly in the specified order.
- Relevant tests pass.

author: theeldermillenial
body:
## Summary

- **Haskell cardano-node 10.4.1 validates and adopts blocks forged by vibe-node** in a 3-node private devnet
- VRF proofs, KES signatures, Babbage/Conway header format, block numbering, and chain selection all pass Haskell validation
- 9 critical bugs found and fixed via systematic comparison against the Haskell forge loop
- Version bump to v0.6.0 with full documentation update

## Key Fixes

### VRF Seed Construction (the critical discovery)
Conway (Praos) uses `mkInputVRF = blake2b(slot_be64 || epochNonce)` — **no XOR with seedL constant**. TPraos `mkSeed` (Shelley-Mary) XORs with a universal constant, but Praos dropped this in favor of a single unified VRF evaluation. Found by reading the vendor submodule: `Praos/VRF.hs` vs `BHeader.hs`.

### NodeKernel Chain Selection
Previously append-only — mixed received and forged blocks into a non-linear chain. Now maintains proper chain selection: received blocks always accepted if better, forged blocks only when they extend the current tip. Fork switching with predecessor tracking.

### 9 Bugs Fixed Total
| Bug | Severity |
|-----|----------|
| VRF seed: Praos mkInputVRF vs TPraos mkSeed | CRITICAL |
| Header format: 10-field Babbage vs 14-field Shelley | CRITICAL |
| Genesis hash: raw bytes vs re-encoded JSON | CRITICAL |
| Block number: real block_number vs slot number | CRITICAL |
| Chain-sync era index: HFC 0-based vs CBOR tag | HIGH |
| Epoch nonce: per-slot refresh vs startup-only | CRITICAL |
| Relative stake: per-slot refresh vs startup-only | HIGH |
| NodeKernel chain: linear chain selection vs append-only | HIGH |
| cbor2 C binding: switched to cbor2pure | HIGH |

## Devnet Results

```
ValidCandidate + AddedToCurrentChain at every block
Zero VRFKeyBadProof
Zero UnexpectedBlockNo
Zero InvalidIntersection
```

## Files Changed (41 commits)
- `packages/vibe-cardano/src/vibe/cardano/forge/leader.py` — Praos mkInputVRF
- `packages/vibe-cardano/src/vibe/cardano/node/kernel.py` — Chain selection
- `packages/vibe-cardano/src/vibe/cardano/node/run.py` — Forge loop fixes
- `packages/vibe-cardano/tests/forge/` — Updated tests
- `docs/` — Phase 5 devlog, milestones, forge-loop-comparison
- `README.md` — v0.6.0, 4,290+ tests, Haskell acceptance

body:
This PR resolves several critical issues encountered when building and running the Golem system within a Docker environment.

### Key Fixes:
1. **TypeScript Build Reliability**: Corrected NODE_ENV management during the multi-stage build process to ensure devDependencies (like TypeScript) are available for transpilation while maintaining production optimizations for the final output.
2. **Next.js Prerendering**: Fixed a 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useState')' error during 'next build' by enforcing NODE_ENV=production during the build command.
3. **Managed Browser Stability**: Switched from system-installed Chromium to Playwright-managed Chromium binaries stored in a persistent path (/app/pw-browsers). This ensures 100% compatibility with Playwright APIs and stealth plugins.
4. **Volume Permission Alignment**: Updated the container user to use the built-in 'node' user (UID/GID 1000) with a proper home directory. This resolves 'Permission Denied' and 'Failed to create directory' errors when using host-mounted volumes for persistence (golem_memory and logs).
5. **Dashboard Static Assets**: Added the missing 'web-dashboard/out' directory to the final image, resolving ENOENT errors when serving the dashboard via static export.
6. **HTTPS Stability**: Added ca-certificates to ensure secure connections to AI services (Gemini) and bot APIs (Discord/Telegram).

These changes ensure that developers can successfully launch the system using a simple 'docker compose up -d --build' command.

author: danilloaraujo
body:
This pull request introduces a new modular "Agent Mesh" architecture for multimodal message processing, where specialized agents handle accessibility, gesture recognition, avatar animation, and orchestration through a central asynchronous bus. Each agent is now decoupled, subscribes to specific message types, and communicates via a shared bus, improving extensibility and maintainability. The pipeline orchestration is handled through a unified interface, and the agent registry and base classes are introduced for easy agent discovery and registration.

**Agent Mesh infrastructure and orchestration:**

* Introduced `AgentRegistry` and `agent_bus` in `agents/__init__.py` to provide a central directory and message bus for all active agent instances, enabling discovery and event routing without direct agent references.
* Added `BaseAgent` abstract class in `agents/base_agent.py` to standardize agent registration, subscription, and event handling, ensuring all agents follow a common contract and are decoupled from each other.
* Implemented `AgentMeshPipeline` in `agents/pipeline.py` to orchestrate the message flow through the agent mesh, publishing initial events and collecting terminal results, with robust timeout handling and message transformation.

**New and refactored agent implementations:**

* Added `AccessibilityAgent` (`agents/accessibility_agent.py`) to enrich messages with accessibility features such as subtitles and TTS audio, and to ensure downstream agents receive correlated events for proper pipeline resolution.
* Added `AvatarAgent` (`agents/avatar_agent.py`) to generate sign-language gloss sequences from sign-adapted text, fan-in correlated accessibility data, and publish the final avatar animation message.
* Added `GestureAgent` (`agents/gesture_agent.py`) to convert gesture recognition events into natural-language transcription messages, allowing gesture input to flow through the same enrichment pipeline as speech.

author: jkweks
body:
## Summary
This PR significantly improves application performance by consolidating multiple database queries into single aggregated queries in the dashboard controller and refactoring frontend DOM rendering to use batch operations instead of incremental innerHTML concatenation.

## Key Changes

### Backend (DashboardController)
- **Consolidated stats queries**: Replaced 4 separate database queries with a single `selectRaw()` query that calculates `skus_tracked`, `units_on_hand`, `low_stock_alerts`, and `critical_count` in one pass
- **Unified committed quantity calculation**: Merged `getCommittedFromFulfillment()` and `calculateCommittedAsPacks()` into a single `calcUnitsCommitted()` method using SQL `CASE` statements for pack/each conversion
- **Database-level sorting for computed fields**: Replaced in-memory sorting for `quantity_committed` and `quantity_available` with correlated subqueries in the `ORDER BY` clause, eliminating the need to fetch all products before pagination
- **Removed redundant endpoints**: Eliminated separate `low_stock`, `critical_stock`, and `committed_parts` response fields from the main `index()` endpoint (data already available in stats)
- **Simplified method signatures**: Added return type hints and removed unused `JobReservation` import

### Frontend (JavaScript)
- **Batch DOM updates**: Changed all `forEach` loops that concatenated to `innerHTML` to use `.map()` with `.join('')` for single DOM write operation
- **Permission checking optimization**: Converted permission array lookups to a `Set` for O(1) lookup time; consolidated three separate permission attribute handlers into unified logic
- **Debounced permission reapplication**: Added 50ms debounce to permission watcher to prevent thrashing during bulk DOM updates
- **Optimized pagination rendering**: Accumulated pagination HTML in array before single `innerHTML` assignment

### Files Modified
- `laravel/app/Http/Controllers/Api/DashboardController.php` - Query consolidation and method refactoring
- `laravel/resources/views/partials/auth-scripts.blade.php` - Permission checking optimization
- `laravel/resources/views/transactions.blade.php` - DOM rendering batch operations
- `laravel/resources/views/admin.blade.php` - DOM rendering batch operations
- `laravel/resources/views/dashboard.blade.php` - DOM rendering batch operations
- `laravel/resources/views/storage-locations.blade.php` - DOM rendering batch operations
- `laravel/resources/views/critical-stock.blade.php` - DOM rendering batch operations
- `laravel/resources/views/low-stock.blade.php` - DOM rendering batch operations

## Performance Impact
- **Database**: Reduced dashboard stats from 4+ queries to 1-2 queries; eliminated need for in-memory sorting of large product sets
- **Frontend**: Eliminated repeated DOM reflows during table rendering; improved permission checking from O(n) to O(1) per element

author: baranidh
body:
Root cause: _fetchAdsbApi and _tryWindow blindly returned whatever the API responded with. Promise.any picked whichever resolved first — even if it was a completely different aircraft (e.g. searching SQ308 returned ARE4064 because adsb.lol responded faster with an unrelated flight).

Fix at 3 layers:
1. _tryWindow: accepts validCallsigns array, finds matching entry in OpenSky results instead of blindly taking the last one
2. _fetchAdsbApi: accepts validCallsigns array, scans ac[] for a matching callsign, rejects with 'callsign mismatch' if none match
3. trackFlightNumber: validates merged result — both record and adsb sources are checked against expected variants before use. Unvalidated sources are discarded, not merged. Shows clear error if both fail.

Also: fetchAdsbLive and fetchFlightRecord now pass the variants array through the entire call chain for end-to-end validation.

author: lxmenm
body:
## 背景

当前 `tf_light_v1` 的主要问题不是评估指标逻辑，而是轻量模型训练产物本身不稳定：

- 默认只保存 legacy `.h5`
- 后续 `load_model()` 容易受到 TF/Keras 版本兼容影响
- 手工 fallback 也会因为结构/权重不一致而失真

因此需要从 **训练产物格式与模型注册路径** 本身进行修复。

## 这次修改

### 1. 训练脚本改为稳定产物
更新 `tomato/train_mobilenetv3_light_v1.py`：

- 默认保存：
  - `models/mobilenetv3_light_v1.keras`
  - `models/mobilenetv3_light_v1.weights.h5`
  - `models/mobilenetv3_light_v1_artifacts.json`
- `mobilenetv3_light_v1_artifacts.json` 中记录：
  - `alpha`
  - `dropout`
  - `image_size`
  - `num_classes`
  - 路径信息
- 可选额外导出 legacy h5：
  - `--export_legacy_h5`

### 2. 推理脚本支持双路径加载
更新 `tomato/infer_mobilenetv3_light_v1.py`：

- 优先加载 `.keras`
- 如果 `.keras` 不存在，则按：
  - `artifacts.json`
  - `weights.h5`
  - 源码重建结构
  - 再加载权重

### 3. 注册表切到稳定路径
更新 `model_registry.py`：

- `tf_light_v1` 的模型路径由
  - `models/densenet121_tomato_disease_model_light_v1.h5`
- 改为
  - `models/mobilenetv3_light_v1.keras`

### 4. 文档同步更新
更新 `tomato/README_light_model.md`：

- 说明新的默认产物
- 说明 legacy h5 是可选导出
- 说明新的验证顺序

## 预期效果

- 重新训练后，`tf_light_v1` 不再依赖脆弱的 legacy `.h5` 作为主入口
- `eval_models` 和推理脚本都能围绕 `.keras + weights + artifacts` 稳定工作
- 后续如果还要做 fallback，也有更明确的结构参数来源

## 推荐验证

先重新训练轻量模型：

```bash
python -m tomato.train_mobilenetv3_light_v1 \
  --head_epochs 8 \
  --fine_tune_epochs 18 \
  --alpha 0.75 \
  --loss focal \
  --focal_gamma 1.5
```

然后重新评估：

```bash
python tools/eval_models.py --data_dir tomato/val --limit 20
```

最后抽查推理：

```bash
python -m tomato.infer_mobilenetv3_light_v1 --image path/to/image.jpg --topk 3
```

body:
# MET-81: Upgrade backlog sync dashboard with multi-select, async loading, filtering, and repo-scoped sync-all config

## Summary
- Linear issue: https://linear.app/metastack-labs/issue/MET-81/upgrade-backlog-sync-dashboard-with-multi-select-async-loading
- Published automatically by `meta agents listen` for `MET-81`

## Lifecycle
- Initial publication uses a draft PR for unattended work in progress.
- The same PR is promoted to ready for review during the existing review handoff.

## Issue Context
# Upgrade backlog sync dashboard with multi-select, async loading, filtering, and repo-scoped sync-all config

Update the Meta backlog sync experience in this repository so users can operate on multiple Linear issues from the dashboard instead of only one issue at a time. The dashboard should render immediately, show loading placeholders for backlog entries while Linear issues are being fetched, support selecting multiple visible issues, expose a top-level `Select all` control that applies to the current filtered result set, and allow filtering Linear issues by status and label.

Add repo-scoped configuration so sync-all behavior can be enabled for this repository through `crate::config::AppConfig` and repo metadata rather than ad hoc environment reads. Preserve existing backlog sync semantics for repositories that do not enable the new repo-scoped sync-all setting, and add targeted tests for command behavior and dashboard state transitions.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Interactive `meta backlog sync` flow allows selecting more than one visible Linear issue before running sync actions, and existing single-selection behavior remains valid as a subset of the new flow.
* The issue list includes a top-level `Select all` control that selects all currently visible issues after active filters and search are applied, without selecting hidden issues outside the current result set.
* Dashboard first paint is no longer blocked on the initial Linear issue fetch: the shell/dashboard state renders first and backlog rows show a loading state until issue data arrives.
* Users can filter the Linear issue list by status and label in the dashboard, and bulk selection operates against the filtered visible result set.
* Repo-scoped configuration supports sync-all behavior through `crate::config::AppConfig` and repo metadata rather than ad hoc environment reads.
* Backlog sync push/pull behavior remains unchanged for repositories that do not enable the new repo-scoped sync-all configuration.
* Command-path validation covers the changed backlog-sync flow, including launch path, selection and filter interactions, expected sync target set, and no-regression handling when Linear returns no issues or fetches slowly.
* Tests cover the async loading state, multi-select and select-all logic, status and label filtering, and repo-scoped config resolution for sync-all behavior.

body:
### Motivation
- The close-job was matching posts by the legacy `event_date` meta which caused posts from other months (e.g. August) to be incorrectly detected while this site treats `post_date` as the event/schedule date.
- Diagnostic logs were not showing `post_date`, making it hard to inspect why matches were missing or unexpected.

body:
## Problem
The admin dashboard showed eBay API as 'unreachable' with a 400 status, even though publishing was working fine all day.

## Root Cause
The health check was pinging eBay's Browse API endpoint without authentication, which correctly returns a 400 error. However, the code only treated 200, 401, and 403 as 'reachable', so 400 was flagged as an error.

## Solution
Updated the eBay API health check to treat **any 2xx-4xx status as reachable**:
- 2xx-3xx: Successful responses
- 4xx: Client errors (but API is responding) - 400 is expected without auth
- 5xx: Actual server outages (flag as unreachable)

## System Checks Overview
The admin dashboard currently checks:
1. **Stripe** - Mode (live/test) and active subscriptions
2. **eBay API** - Reachability via Browse API ping
3. **Gemini AI** - Usage stats (calls, tokens, costs)
4. **Total Users** - User count in profiles table
5. **Feature Usage** - Analytics for AI analysis, publishing, etc.
6. **Cost Alerts** - Last sent alert timestamp and details

body:
Closes #18

## Summary

Adds `@voltagent/redis` — a new `StorageAdapter` backed by Redis (via `ioredis`) for fast, in-memory persistence of agent memory.

## What it does

```typescript
import { RedisMemoryAdapter } from "@voltagent/redis";

const memory = new RedisMemoryAdapter({
  connection: "redis://localhost:6379",
  keyPrefix: "voltagent",
  debug: false,
});
```

Implements the full `StorageAdapter` interface:
- **Conversations** — CRUD with sorted set indexes by resource, user, and global
- **Messages** — stored in sorted sets ordered by timestamp (efficient range queries)
- **Working memory** — simple key-value, scoped to conversation or user
- **Workflow state** — full lifecycle with suspended state tracking via Redis sets
- **Conversation steps** — ordered by timestamp in sorted sets

## Design decisions

- `ioredis` over `redis` (better TypeScript support, pipeline API, cluster-ready)
- Sorted sets for messages/steps (natural time ordering, range queries)
- Pipeline batching for atomic multi-key operations
- `safeStringify` for all serialization (per project convention)
- Key prefix configurable (default: `voltagent`)

author: copilot
body:
This updates `using` parsing to match the TC39 explicit resource management semantics in loop headers. In particular, `using` now works in classic `for` initializers, while invalid `for-in`/`for-of` forms remain rejected.

- **Spec-aligned loop handling**
  - Allow `using` declarations in classic `for` initializer clauses.
  - Preserve rejection of `using` as the declaration form in `for-in` and `for-of`.
  - Keep `using` requiring an initializer in `for` headers.

- **Parser disambiguation**
  - Extend `for`-header parsing to treat `using` as a lexical declaration starter where the spec allows it.
  - Keep identifier/expression behavior intact for non-declaration forms.
  - Tighten `await using` parsing so declaration forms are recognized without misparsing expression forms like `await using()`.

- **Coverage**
  - Add focused loop tests for:
    - valid classic `for (using ...; ...; ...)`
    - rejected `for (using ... in ...)`
    - rejected `for (using ... of ...)`
  - Add a regression test for `await using()` being parsed as an expression, not a declaration.

Example:

```js
for (using resource = acquire(); keepGoing(); advance()) {
  work(resource);
}

for (using x in xs) {}   // rejected
for (using x of xs) {}   // rejected

async function f() {
  await using handle = open();
  await using(); // expression, not a declaration
}
```

## Overview

This PR has two goals:
1. **Wire up Azure Application Insights** for traffic/telemetry tracking using a GitHub Secret
2. **Remove all PII** (home address and phone number) from every page — keep only first name, last name, and email address

## Part 1 — Application Insights

### 1a. Add NuGet package to `PortfolioDemo/PortfolioDemo.csproj`

Add this inside the existing `<ItemGroup>` that has `PackageReference` entries:
```xml
<PackageReference Include="Microsoft.ApplicationInsights.AspNetCore" Version="2.22.0" />

### 1b. Update `PortfolioDemo/Program.cs`

After `builder.Services.AddRazorPages();` and `builder.Services.AddControllers();`, add:
```csharp
// Add Application Insights telemetry
builder.Services.AddApplicationInsightsTelemetry();
```

The full updated `Program.cs` should look like:
```csharp
var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args);

// Add services to the container.
builder.Services.AddRazorPages();
builder.Services.AddControllers();

// Add Application Insights telemetry
builder.Services.AddApplicationInsightsTelemetry();

var app = builder.Build();

// Configure the HTTP request pipeline.
if (!app.Environment.IsDevelopment())
{
    app.UseExceptionHandler("/Error");
    // The default HSTS value is 30 days. You may want to change this for production scenarios, see https://aka.ms/aspnetcore-hsts.
    app.UseHsts();
}

app.UseHttpsRedirection();
app.UseStaticFiles();

app.UseRouting();

app.UseAuthorization();

app.MapControllers();
app.MapRazorPages();

app.Run();
```

### 1c. Update `PortfolioDemo/appsettings.json`

Add the Application Insights connection string config. It should read from the environment variable `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` (which is how Azure Web Apps and GitHub Actions secrets inject it). The `appsettings.json` should have a placeholder:

```json
{
  "Logging": {
    "LogLevel": {
      "Default": "Information",
      "Microsoft.AspNetCore": "Warning"
    }
  },
  "AllowedHosts": "*",
  "ApplicationInsights": {
    "ConnectionString": ""
  }
}
```

> Note: The actual value will come from the environment variable `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` set as a GitHub Secret and injected into the Azure Web App's application settings. Do NOT hardcode the connection string.

### 1d. Update the GitHub Actions workflow `.github/workflows/main_monicarivera-portfolio-demo.yml`

In the `deploy` job, add the Application Insights connection string as an app setting during deployment. Update the `azure/webapps-deploy@v3` step to pass the secret, OR add a step before it to set the app setting. 

Add a step in the `deploy` job after downloading the artifact, using the `azure/appservice-settings` action OR by adding the connection string as an environment variable reference. 

Actually, the cleanest approach for Azure Web Apps is to add it as an **app setting** in the Azure Portal (Settings → Configuration → Application settings → add `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` with the value from the secret). 

Instead, update the workflow to document this with a comment, and add the `APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING` secret reference in the workflow for future use:

In the `deploy` job, add an environment variable:
```yaml
deploy:
  runs-on: windows-latest
  needs: build
  env:
    APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING: ${{ secrets.APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING }}
```

This pull request introduces a comprehensive Advertisement Marketplace feature across the backend and frontend, allowing customers to request advertisements and admins/owners to manage and promote ads, including banner uploads and live promotions. It updates API routes, documentation, database schema, and user interfaces to support these workflows, and adds a new public Marketplace page to the frontend.

**Backend: Advertisement Marketplace and API Enhancements**
- Added new public and admin advertisement endpoints, including support for public ad requests, admin review, creation, update (with banner upload), and deletion. Updated OpenAPI docs and schemas to reflect these changes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a54d2dad1be5eea9e70f8514ae65d89b65357120a312bfb9f644ddeb1844ca0dL222-R222) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a54d2dad1be5eea9e70f8514ae65d89b65357120a312bfb9f644ddeb1844ca0dR256-R266) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-c66e8f76215056106920462e59ace46ae2dcd364f8d602786b8d315d012c0694R234-R260) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-993e9d054a7df643eb8fb0b74bafbfc7b8a258d0d70d45b24984f82fb18a6ddfR45-R46) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-1f7258489cd206e12c199da85b9bbbb80a1f71e8321b1d376563a64f2ddeb7adR1-R168)
- Modified database schema and service logic to support ad request workflow, new status values (`requested`, `live`, `inactive`), and optional image uploads. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b6b474f33d838c05691eeb53c27a9fbb17dec1fc4cf9a9d3e51ae36b5352bf94L7-R11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-0a70e24a57ed80d4a4809bd68fe60aab92e20c28e3c3026e7d89e4f06ab942dfL10-R10) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-0a70e24a57ed80d4a4809bd68fe60aab92e20c28e3c3026e7d89e4f06ab942dfL20-R25) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-0d6678144ffa8eb9e5ff415c9422d3dad38bdc57d7f12e86abd3aedf15cdf3c1R36-R50)
- Updated backend documentation for new endpoints and clarified advertisement API usage. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a54d2dad1be5eea9e70f8514ae65d89b65357120a312bfb9f644ddeb1844ca0dL222-R222) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a54d2dad1be5eea9e70f8514ae65d89b65357120a312bfb9f644ddeb1844ca0dR256-R266)

**Frontend: Marketplace Page and Navigation**
- Added a new public `/marketplace` route and page, listing live advertisements and allowing users to submit ad requests. Updated navigation (`Navbar`) to include the Marketplace link, with correct handling for hash and non-hash routes. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-35aa98d245b201cfc92c74313abcf8fa0f6069fc750f05e7a755665360a0e543R156) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a0eba768ed9d2a17091f82d46efb5e1c988f08185cc1e9989366995cdb4e3ba9R56-R57) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-a0eba768ed9d2a17091f82d46efb5e1c988f08185cc1e9989366995cdb4e3ba9R69) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-3990a18cf99be7d0c688f4b319ea1214e2eade9aff1f34efde27dd4a0b0476edR32) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-3990a18cf99be7d0c688f4b319ea1214e2eade9aff1f34efde27dd4a0b0476edR72) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-3990a18cf99be7d0c688f4b319ea1214e2eade9aff1f34efde27dd4a0b0476edR82-R91) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-3990a18cf99be7d0c688f4b319ea1214e2eade9aff1f34efde27dd4a0b0476edR166) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-3990a18cf99be7d0c688f4b319ea1214e2eade9aff1f34efde27dd4a0b0476edR175-R184)
- Updated documentation to describe the new Marketplace page, its features, and how it integrates into the landing page and admin workflows. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-35aa98d245b201cfc92c74313abcf8fa0f6069fc750f05e7a755665360a0e543L297-R298) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-35aa98d245b201cfc92c74313abcf8fa0f6069fc750f05e7a755665360a0e543L323-R324) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-35aa98d245b201cfc92c74313abcf8fa0f6069fc750f05e7a755665360a0e543L335-R336)

**Admin/Owner Advertisement Management**
- Enhanced the admin interface to support reviewing requested advertisements, promoting them to live status, and managing banner uploads. Updated UI icons and state management to reflect new ad statuses and workflows. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-522fc7a678c2a517e4059579a9ec33f74d95e9937aafd021bef8940da3b6f8aaL20-R22) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-522fc7a678c2a517e4059579a9ec33f74d95e9937aafd021bef8940da3b6f8aaR39)

**General Documentation and Versioning**
- Updated project version and last updated date to reflect the new release. Clarified user role capabilities and summarized new advertisement management features in the documentation. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L116-R119) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L256-R257)

**API Route and Middleware Adjustments**
- Updated backend routes to support new advertisement endpoints and ensured correct middleware usage for public and admin routes.

These changes collectively enable a full-featured advertisement marketplace, supporting both customer-driven ad requests and robust admin management, with clear documentation and user interface improvements.

author: biwashi
body:
## 概要

`bin/prepare-track.sh` における demucs コマンド呼び出し時のシェルクォーティングバグを修正します。

## 問題

- `DEMUCS_CMD` 変数にダブルクォート内でシングルクォートを含む文字列（`"uvx --with 'numpy<2' demucs"`）を代入していた
- `$DEMUCS_CMD` を展開実行すると、シングルクォートがリテラル文字としてそのまま `uvx` に渡される
- 結果として `uvx` が `'numpy<2'`（クォート付き）をパッケージ名として解釈し、「Expected package name starting with an alphanumeric character」エラーが発生

## 修正内容

- `DEMUCS_CMD` 文字列変数を `run_demucs()` 関数に置き換え
- 関数内でダブルクォート `"numpy<2"` を使用することで、`<` がリダイレクトとして解釈されず、かつクォート文字がリテラルに渡されることもない
- `$@` による引数の受け渡しで、引数のクォーティングも正しく保持される

## テスト計画

- [ ] `uvx` がインストールされた環境で `prepare-track.sh` を実行し、demucs が正常に呼び出されることを確認
- [ ] `uv tool run` フォールバック時も同様に動作することを確認
- [ ] `demucs` が直接インストールされている場合の動作確認
- [ ] `--skip-demucs` オプションが引き続き正常に動作することを確認

author: warleynutricionista-jpg
body:
### Motivation
- World detection was re-discovering platform props created by the resource, causing duplicated lift entries and mixed interactions between `config`/`custom`/`world` lifts.  The goal was to ensure 1 cadastro = 1 elevador and full isolation. 
- Each lift must expose a friendly name, stable identity and its own state (vehicle, attachments, menus/targets) to avoid contamination and incorrect commands.
- Removing a vehicle must only release it (unfreeze/unlink) without teleporting or forcing position changes.

### Description
- Prevent world-scan duplicates by ignoring entities already managed by the resource and by deduping discovered world lifts near existing configured/custom lifts; add `isManagedLiftEntity` and proximity dedupe. (client: `client/lift.lua`, server: `server/lift_admin.lua`)
- Add friendly `liftName` lifecycle: editor prompt, `normalizeLiftName`/validation, `isDuplicateLiftName` checks, persisted in layouts and synchronized to clients; provide `VRS.GetLiftDisplayName` utility. (server: `server/lift_admin.lua`, shared: `shared/utils.lua`, client: `client/lift_admin.lua`)
- Make lift state fully per-lift: include `liftId`, `liftName` and `vehicleAttachment` (forward/lateral/vertical/heading offsets) in server state and send to clients; clients apply vehicle offsets when moving/attaching a vehicle to the platform. (server: `server/lifts.lua`, client: `client/lift.lua`)
- Remove teleport-on-release: `RemoveFromLift` now only unfreezes/unlinks the vehicle and clears lift state (no `SetEntityCoords` teleport). (client: `client/duty.lua`, server state handling in `server/lifts.lua`)
- Isolate menus/targets per-lift and show friendly names: ox_target entries, NUI and context menus were updated to use `liftName` and unique menu ids per lift; repair/upgrade menus reorganized into contextual, categorized submenus to simplify workflow. (client: `client/target.lua`, `client/duty.lua`, `client/repairs.lua`, `client/upgrades.lua`, `client/lift_admin.lua`)
- Files modified: `shared/utils.lua`, `client/lift.lua`, `server/lifts.lua`, `server/lift_admin.lua`, `client/lift_admin.lua`, `client/target.lua`, `client/duty.lua`, `client/repairs.lua`, `client/upgrades.lua`.

### Testing
- Ran repository sanity checks: `git diff --check` and `git status` (no whitespace or index issues detected) — succeeded. 
- Per-file load attempts with Lua bytechecker (`luac -p`) and executing `loadfile` were attempted but the execution environment does not provide a Lua interpreter/`luac`, so full automated Lua syntax verification could not be completed in this environment. 
- Manual static inspection and multiple local readbacks of modified files were performed to validate the applied changes and ensure consistent references between server and client code (no dangling references found in the changed set).

author: kingscott
body:
## Summary

Adds configuration for miniflux feed polling frequency to reduce noise from high-volume feeds like HackerNews and Reddit.

- Sets `POLLING_FREQUENCY=1440` (24 hours) instead of the default 60 minutes
- Configurable via environment variable (defaults to 1440 in .env.example)
- Per-feed entry limits must be configured individually in the UI

## Manual Steps

After deployment, configure individual feeds:
1. Navigate to **Feeds** → select feed → **Edit**
2. Set **"Maximum number of entries to keep"** to desired limit (e.g., 10)
3. Save

This per-feed limit cannot be set globally via environment variables in miniflux.

## Testing

After deploying with `docker compose up -d`:
```bash
docker exec miniflux miniflux -config-dump | grep -i polling
```

Or verify in the miniflux UI: **Settings** → **About** shows next scheduled refresh time.

- [x] 깃헙 저장소가 공유됐나요?
- 제출하시는 PR이 어떤 PR인지 선택해주세요.
  - [x] 이 PR은 `기능구현 PR` 입니다.
  - [x] 이 PR은 `리팩토링 PR` 입니다.

## 😊 과제 평가자에게 하고 싶은 말

### 청소와 설계를 분리해서 접근했습니다

리팩토링을 시작하기 전에 크게 두 단계로 나눠서 생각했습니다.

**첫 번째는 청소.** 코드를 읽으면서 느낀 문제점들을 먼저 정리했습니다.

- 중복 선언된 constants, util 함수, 타입 정의 → single source of truth 위반
- try-catch가 UI 컴포넌트에 산재되어 있어서 컴포넌트의 관심사가 흐려짐
- 하나의 파일에 너무 많은 로직이 들어있어 한눈에 코드 흐름을 읽기 어려움

**두 번째는 설계.** 근데 중요한 건 그 다음이었습니다. 단순히 코드를 정리하는 것만으로는 부족하고, UX가 실제로 어떤지, 앞으로 어떤 기능이 추가될 수 있는지를 먼저 생각해봐야 더 제대로 된 구조가 나온다고 판단했습니다.

### UX 관점에서 빠른 예약 기능을 먼저 설계했습니다

처음 앱을 써보면서 느낀 가장 큰 불편은, 타임라인에서 "3시에 토스홀 비네" 하고 확인해도 예약 페이지로 가면 그 정보를 다시 필터링해야 한다는 점이었습니다. 보통 회의실 예약은 시간을 미리 정해두고 검색하기보다, 타임라인을 보면서 비어있는 시간 중 사람들이 가능한 시간에 맞춰 고르는 게 자연스러운 흐름이니까요.

그래서 타임라인에서 빈 시간을 클릭 두 번으로 바로 예약할 수 있는 기능을 추가했습니다. 이 기능이 가능하려면 기존 예약 페이지의 폼 로직과 모달의 폼 로직이 겹칠 수밖에 없었고, 그래서 `useBookingForm`으로 폼 상태를 통합 관리하도록 먼저 추상화했습니다. 처음에는 URL 동기화(`useBookingUrlSync`)도 분리해서 뺐다가, 해당 페이지에서만 쓰이니 co-location 원칙에 따라 그냥 페이지 컴포넌트 안에 두기로 했습니다.

이 외에도 예약 수정 기능이나 특정 시간 반복 예약 같은 기능이 추가되더라도 무리 없이 확장할 수 있도록 구조를 잡으려 했습니다. 예를 들어:
- 예약 수정: `useBookingForm`의 `initialState`에 기존 예약 데이터를 넣으면 수정 폼으로 재사용 가능
- 반복 예약: `useCreateReservation`의 mutation 파라미터에 반복 옵션만 추가하면 되고, 에러/성공 메시지 처리는 이미 훅 내부에서 일관되게 관리되고 있음
- 새 모달 추가: `useOverlay`로 선언적으로 열 수 있어서, 예약 상세 보기나 수정 모달도 같은 패턴으로 확장 가능

### 메시지와 에러 처리를 중앙화했습니다

빠른 예약 기능을 모달로 구현하면서, 기존 `location.state` 방식으로는 같은 페이지 내에서 메시지를 표시할 수 없는 문제가 생겼습니다. 페이지 이동 없이 모달에서 예약이 완료되니까요. 이걸 계기로 `MessageContext`를 도입해서 메시지 처리를 중앙화했습니다.

- query 훅 내부에서 `onSuccess`/`onError`에 따른 `showMessage` 호출을 일관되게 처리
- UI 컴포넌트는 메시지를 보여주는 것에만 집중하고, 에러 판단 로직을 모름
- 개별 훅에서 잡지 못하는 에러는 `QueryClient`의 `QueryCache`/`MutationCache`에서 글로벌하게 처리

### Suspense를 도입했습니다

로딩 처리도 중앙화하고 싶었고, 컴포넌트가 "데이터가 항상 있는 환경"에서만 동작할 수 있도록 만들고 싶어서 react-query의 `suspense: true` 옵션을 도입했습니다.

### 구조 컨벤션은 프로젝트 기존 설정을 따랐습니다

처음에 `domains/` 폴더를 만들어서 도메인 레이어를 분리하려 했는데, `vite.config`와 `tsconfig`에 이미 `models/`, `hooks/`, `utils/`, `constants/` 같은 alias가 정의되어 있는 걸 보고, 이 프로젝트가 선호하는 컨벤션을 따르기로 결정했습니다. 단일 도메인(예약) 앱에서 굳이 `domains/reservation/`을 만드는 건 과한 구조라고 판단했습니다.

## 💭 아래는 과제 제출 후에 자유롭게 작성해주세요

**과제를 수행하는데 어려움은 없었나요?**

1. 분리하다 보니 form 상태의 일부이긴 하지만 `floors`처럼 rooms 데이터에서 파생되는 값은 `useBookingForm` 안에 넣기 애매해서 고민이 됐습니다. rooms 데이터에 의존하게 되면 훅의 책임이 커지니까, 결국 파생값은 컴포넌트에서 계산하고 폼 훅은 순수한 폼 상태만 관리하도록 했습니다. 그런데 더 좋은 방법이 있을지 여전히 고민되었습니다.

2. Suspense를 도입하면서 loading 처리를 완전히 중앙화하고 싶었는데, mutation의 loading은 Suspense가 잡지 못해서 완전한 통일이 안 됐습니다. 이전 프로젝트에서 `useIsFetching`/`useIsMutating`으로 전역 오버레이를 만들어 쓴 적이 있는데, `invalidateQueries` 후 refetch마다 오버레이가 뜨면서 오히려 UX를 해치게 되더라고요. 결국 Suspense는 초기 로딩만, mutation loading은 개별 버튼에서 처리하는 방식으로 분리했는데, 이러면 개발자마다 mutation loading 처리를 놓칠 수 있는 여지가 남아서 찜찜합니다. 토스에서는 이 부분을 어떻게 처리하고 있는지 궁금합니다.

**좋았던 점 / 아쉬웠던 점 / 제안하고 싶은 점**

1. 리팩토링하면서 최근 실무에서도 비슷하게 고민했던 부분들이 다시 나왔는데, 이 과제를 통해 피드백을 받을 수 있다는 점이 좋았습니다. 특히 로딩 중앙화 전략, 폼 상태 추상화 범위, 파생 상태의 위치 같은 것들은 정답이 뚜렷하지 않아서, 토스에서는 어떤 기준으로 판단하는지 들어보고 싶습니다.

**제출하는 PR이 `리팩토링 PR`인 경우, 어떤 부분에 초점을 맞춰서 리팩토링했는지 설명해주세요.**

1. **유지보수에 유리한 구조**: 파일을 수정할 때 그 파일만 보면 되는 구조를 목표로 했습니다. 관심사 분리, co-location, 공유 시점에 승격하는 원칙을 일관되게 적용했습니다.
2. **에러/메시지 처리 3계층화**: mutation 훅 내부 → QueryClient 글로벌 핸들러 → 컴포넌트(UI만). 새로운 mutation이 추가돼도 패턴이 동일합니다.
3. **Suspense 도입**: 초기 로딩을 선언적으로 처리하고, 컴포넌트가 데이터 존재를 보장받는 환경을 만들었습니다.
4. **UX 개선**: 타임라인에서 빈 시간을 클릭해 바로 예약하는 기능을 추가하면서, 이를 기존 구조에 자연스럽게 녹이는 데 집중했습니다.

**제출하는 PR이 `기능구현 PR`인 경우, 추가한 기능을 설명해주세요.**

### 타임라인 빠른 예약 기능

타임라인에서 빈 시간을 클릭 두 번으로 바로 예약할 수 있는 기능을 추가했습니다.

**동작 방식:**
1. 타임라인의 빈 영역을 클릭하면 시작 시간이 설정됩니다 (선택 중인 슬롯이 하이라이트)
2. 두 번째 빈 영역을 클릭하면 종료 시간이 설정되고, 바로 예약 모달이 열립니다
3. 모달에서 참석 인원, 장비, 선호 층을 선택하고 예약할 수 있습니다
4. 조건에 따라 예약 가능한 회의실이 자동으로 필터링됩니다

**데모 영상:**

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/147ef0cf-05f8-4e9b-b63d-cca9d96c5966



**구현 포인트:**
- `useTimelineSelection`: 2클릭 시작/종료 시간 선택 로직을 훅으로 분리
- `BookingModal`: 기존 `useBookingForm`을 재사용해서 예약 페이지와 동일한 폼 로직 공유
- `useOverlay`: 토스 스타일 overlay 시스템으로 모달을 선언적으로 관리
- 기존 테스트 26개 모두 통과, 새 기능에 대한 테스트 8개 추가

body:
## Summary
This PR addresses two issues in the dashboard: crashes in the Movement view when loading workout data, and memory pressure on iOS during initial page load.

## Key Changes

- **Movement view robustness**: Added error handling for check-in data loading and fallback logic for gym_split/female_gym_split programs that lack WORKOUT_DB entries
  - Wrapped `dbHelpers.checkins.get()` in try-catch to gracefully handle missing check-in data
  - Added fallback to 'gym' program when gym_split variants are not found in WORKOUT_DB
  - Added null checks and default values for workout schedule to prevent TypeError crashes
  - Applied these fixes to both the conditional and standard program loading paths

- **iOS memory optimization**: Increased script-3 defer delay from 0ms to 300ms on iOS Safari
  - Allows garbage collector more time to reclaim temporary parsing data and retained textures
  - Updated comments to clarify that script-3's `_onReady` helper safely handles cases where DOMContentLoaded has already fired
  - Reduces peak memory usage during HTML parsing on iOS devices

## Implementation Details

The Movement view crash occurred because gym_split users on iOS could open the view before WORKOUT_LIBRARY finished loading (2000ms vs 500ms), causing `heroProg.schedule` to throw a TypeError when `heroProg` was undefined. The fix uses a fallback program lookup and defensive checks before accessing nested properties.

The iOS memory improvement leverages the existing `_onReady` pattern to safely defer script-3 loading, giving the garbage collector a meaningful window to clean up temporary objects created during DOM parsing.

body:
## Summary
This PR closes the remaining frontend contract drift left after PR-13B.

It updates `robots.contract.test.ts` so the share-page noindex assertion matches the new `seo_surface_v1` consumer shape instead of the pre-13B route-local implementation.

## Problem
PR-13B moved share-page metadata authority to backend-owned `seo_surface_v1`, with the old `publicSurface.robotsPolicy` logic kept only as a fallback when the SEO surface is missing.

The implementation was correct, but `robots.contract.test.ts` was still asserting the old string shape:
- direct `robotsPolicy` variable naming
- direct `noindex: robotsPolicy.includes("noindex")`

That left the frontend contract suite red even though the actual route logic had already been migrated.

## What Changed
- Updated `tests/contracts/robots.contract.test.ts`
- The contract now asserts:
  - the share page passes `seoSurface: viewModel.seoSurface`
  - the `noindex` fallback only applies when `seo_surface_v1` is absent
- No runtime code changed

## Validation
- `pnpm vitest run tests/contracts`

Result:
- `59 passed`
- `288 passed tests`

## Scope Guardrails
- Frontend-only
- Test-only
- No runtime behavior changes
- No SEO authority expansion beyond the already-merged PR-13B implementation

# MET-89: Technical: Extract shared agent-session orchestration primitives for listen and review flows

## Summary
- Linear issue: https://linear.app/metastack-labs/issue/MET-89/technical-extract-shared-agent-session-orchestration-primitives-for
- Published automatically by `meta agents listen` for `MET-89`

## Lifecycle
- Initial publication uses a draft PR for unattended work in progress.
- The same PR is promoted to ready for review during the existing review handoff.

## Issue Context
# Technical: Extract shared agent-session orchestration primitives for listen and review flows

## Parent Issue

* Identifier: `MET-85`
* Title: Extract shared agent-session orchestration primitives for listen and review flows
* URL: [MET-85](https://linear.app/metastack-labs/issue/MET-85/extract-shared-agent-session-orchestration-primitives-for-listen-and)

## Context

MetaStack CLI already has one mature unattended workflow in `src/listen/` and a second review-oriented orchestration surface in `src/orchestrate/`. Both manage durable session state, summarize long-running work for operators, and coordinate stateful automation over multiple polling cycles or worker turns. Today those concerns are implemented separately: `ListenProjectStore` couples install-scoped project identity, lock handling, state persistence, and detail artifacts in one place, while `OrchestratePaths` plus the surrounding save/load helpers independently manage repo-local session directories, current-session pointers, review records, staging state, and event logs.

The duplication is still partial rather than one-to-one, which is exactly why this slice should stay disciplined. The value is not a generic framework. The value is a smaller shared runtime layer that keeps filesystem layout, active-session ownership, and summary shaping coherent across agent-backed long-running commands while leaving ticket-pickup, review heuristics, backlog classification, and staging behavior where they belong.

## Proposed Approach

Introduce a crate-local shared session-runtime module that supports two storage scopes: install-scoped workflow stores and repo-local workflow stores. Move only the reusable infrastructure into that module: root/layout description, JSON persistence helpers with contextual errors, active-session ownership helpers that can represent both lock files and current-session pointers, and status-summary helpers for structurally identical metadata.

Adopt the shared layer in `src/listen/` first for store and detail-artifact plumbing, then in `src/orchestrate/` for session directory management and record IO. Reuse summary helpers in `src/listen/dashboard.rs` and `src/orchestrate/dashboard.rs` only where they preserve current user-visible output. Keep command-specific enums, review decisions, staging merge rules, workpad handling, and worker behavior local to their feature modules.

## Scope

In scope:

* Shared internal runtime primitives used by `src/listen/` and review-side orchestration in `src/orchestrate/`
* Persisted session layout helpers, ownership semantics, record IO, and summary shaping
* Migration of current listen and orchestrate consumers to the shared layer
* Tests and documentation proving no regression in CLI behavior or persisted data layout

Out of scope:

* Renaming `meta agents orchestrate` or introducing a new public `meta agents review` command in this slice
* Collapsing command-specific phase enums into one universal state machine
* Changing listen ticket workflow rules, review suppression rules, or staging merge policy
* Broad module reorganization outside the extraction needed for the shared runtime layer

## Risks

* Shared abstractions can easily become too generic and pull command-specific logic into the wrong layer.
* Listen and orchestrate store state in different roots, so a shared persistence layer must not accidentally force a migration.
* Status and dashboard output are easy to regress when summary shaping is centralized.

## Validation

- [ ] `cargo test listen::store`
- [ ] `cargo test listen::dashboard`
- [ ] `cargo test orchestrate::state`
- [ ] `cargo test orchestrate::review`
- [ ] `cargo test orchestrate::dashboard`
- [ ] `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- [ ] `make quality`
- [ ] Record stable filesystem-layout and status-output proofs in [`validation.md`](<./validation.md>)

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Scope and non-goals clearly distinguish shared runtime primitives from feature-specific business rules.
- [ ] The implementation plan names the concrete repo paths to migrate in `src/listen/` and `src/orchestrate/`.
- [ ] A shared internal abstraction exists for persisted session layout and active-session ownership semantics used by both workflow families.
- [ ] Structurally identical summary shaping is moved behind shared helpers without changing user-visible CLI output.
- [ ] Existing listen and orchestrate tests pass, and new targeted tests cover the extracted shared layer.
- [ ] Validation evidence is recorded in [`validation.md`](<./validation.md>) and linked artifacts.

body:
Adds a deterministic, blocking provenance validation gate that must pass before any temporal or epistemic execution. Implements the TRIZEL Provenance Gate contract with strict binary outcomes (`VALID` / `INVALID`) and full abort on any failure.

## New files

- **`validation/provenance_validator.py`** — Core gate logic
  - `validate_observations(roots)` → structured batch report
  - `abort_if_invalid(report)` → stderr + `sys.exit(1)` on any `INVALID`
  - Enforces all 5 canonical failure modes: `provenance_missing`, `source_unverifiable`, `hash_mismatch`, `derived_data_detected`, `cross_day_dependency_detected`

- **`scripts/run_provenance_check.py`** — Standalone CLI entry point
  - Accepts one or more `--observation-root DIR` arguments
  - Emits machine-readable JSON report to stdout; exits `0` (all valid), `1` (gate fail), `2` (bad args)

## Validation contract (per observation)

Each `data/observations/YYYY-MM-DD/normalized_observation.json` must satisfy:

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| `provenance.provenance_root` | exactly `AUTO-DZ-ACT-3I-ATLAS-DAILY` |
| `provenance.snapshot_id` | matches `snapshot-YYYY-MM-DD-audited` |
| `provenance.sha256` | 64 lower-case hex digits |
| `provenance.manifest_ref` | non-empty string |
| `provenance.doi` / `doi_absent` | value present **or** `doi_absent: true` |
| `derived`, `reused_data`, `cross_day` | must all be absent/false |

## Example

```python
from validation.provenance_validator import validate_observations, abort_if_invalid

report = validate_observations(["data/observations/2026-03-21"])
# {
#   "batch_outcome": "INVALID",
#   "observations": [{"outcome": "INVALID", "failures": ["provenance_missing"]}]
# }
abort_if_invalid(report)  # prints to stderr, exits 1
```

```bash
python scripts/run_provenance_check.py --observation-root data/observations/2026-03-21
# exits 1 — existing observations lack provenance block
```

body:
This pull request prepares for the `0.1.0-beta.6` pre-release of the NoSuckShell desktop app and introduces several new backend capabilities. The most significant changes include version bumps across multiple files, the addition of a local license management and verification system, support for custom SSH directory locations, and enhancements to host metadata for improved SSH key policy handling.

**Release and Dependency Updates**
- Bumped version numbers from `0.1.0-beta.5` to `0.1.0-beta.6` in `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `Cargo.toml`, documentation, and issue templates to mark the new pre-release. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f260cda9a89e97068b04d6627600f3e650fcff63642da2f62c7b9412a2da2646L3-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f4eec9a7ef4162effebbca47dc2b4fad550681464de39eef3b9ec9c29ff34c86L3-R13) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-82930813b4ae32e116b1b66001712308d672447e262217e9b6f3b72342335675L3-R3) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b335630551682c19a781afebcf4d07bf978fb1f8ac04c6bf87428ed5106870f5L96-R102) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-185833cb26d7ac66a4d39042fd576a820c2c2c6d05ad18973bb9c7dce77267c5L9-R9)
- Added new dependencies for both frontend (`@tauri-apps/plugin-dialog`) and backend (e.g., `ssh2`, `ed25519-dalek`, `fs2`, `hex`, `tauri-plugin-dialog`, `dirs`, `uzers`) to support new features and plugins. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-f260cda9a89e97068b04d6627600f3e650fcff63642da2f62c7b9412a2da2646R23-R34) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f4eec9a7ef4162effebbca47dc2b4fad550681464de39eef3b9ec9c29ff34c86R870-R878) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-82930813b4ae32e116b1b66001712308d672447e262217e9b6f3b72342335675R16-R35)

**License Management**
- Introduced a new `license.rs` backend module that enables offline Ed25519 license verification and local license file storage, including activation, validation, and entitlement checks.
- Added commands and data structures to support license status queries and activation through the backend.

**SSH Directory and Configuration Enhancements**
- Implemented support for custom SSH directory locations by refactoring all code that previously assumed `~/.ssh` to use a new `ssh_home::effective_ssh_dir()` function. This affects host metadata, layout profiles, and adds new IPC commands for getting and setting SSH directory overrides. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9f86536c64036e03e6ca998d32b0ee9c56e540187cfb7e48f3ed1a591286f696L35-R89) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-897268904fce92dcf6ac4243ac807ebd4ed94aa69eae6395171ffea3e133b397L58-R58) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-981e94b5aacd53518a6fc29b19f08f1be3643bc45d872174176ec3652586fd2dR98-R117)
- Added backend commands to get and set the raw SSH config, and to retrieve SSH directory info.

**Host Metadata and SSH Key Policy**
- Enhanced `HostMetadata` to support `trust_host_default` and an explicit `strictHostKeyPolicy` field (with migration logic), allowing more granular control over SSH host key checking policies. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9f86536c64036e03e6ca998d32b0ee9c56e540187cfb7e48f3ed1a591286f696R7-R26) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-9f86536c64036e03e6ca998d32b0ee9c56e540187cfb7e48f3ed1a591286f696R35-R68)
- Added logic for resolving the effective `StrictHostKeyChecking` policy for hosts, improving security and user experience.

**Backend Refactoring and Plugin Support**
- Modularized the backend by introducing new modules (`license`, `plugins`, `sftp_export`, `quick_ssh`, `sftp`, `ssh_home`) and reorganizing imports and command wiring in `main.rs` for better maintainability and clarity. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-981e94b5aacd53518a6fc29b19f08f1be3643bc45d872174176ec3652586fd2dR1-R18) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-981e94b5aacd53518a6fc29b19f08f1be3643bc45d872174176ec3652586fd2dR28-R67)
- Added support for new Tauri plugin dialog permissions in the app's capabilities configuration.

These changes collectively improve the app's flexibility, security, and readiness for broader testing in the upcoming beta release.

body:
The venda form had a single static pair of buyer fields; it now generates one `donaterPhone`/`donaterName` row per ticket in the ticketbook when the user leaves the `ticketbookNumber` field, and prefills those rows if the ticketbook already exists in the backend.

## Model & service

- **`ticketbook.dto.ts`**: Added `TicketSellData` (`number`, `donaterName`, `donaterPhone`) and `TicketbookWithTickets` (extends `Ticketbook` with `tickets: TicketSellData[]`).
- **`ticketbook.service.ts`**: Added `getTicketbookInformation(idInstitution, idLottery, number)` — `GET /institution/{id}/lottery/{id}/ticketbook/information?number={n}`, returns `null` on 404/error via `catchError`.

## Component (`venda`)

- Replaced static `ticketNumber`/`donaterName`/`donaterPhone` controls with a `tickets` `FormArray`.
- `buildTicketRows()` implements the specified formula:
  ```ts
  const base = (ticketbookNumber - 1) * numTicketsTicketbook;
  for (let i = 1; base + i <= ticketbookNumber * numTicketsTicketbook; i++) { … }
  ```
  producing exactly `numTicketsTicketbook` rows with auto-computed ticket numbers.
- `onTicketbookNumberBlur()` drives both row generation and the API lookup; if the API returns an existing ticketbook, each row is prefilled with its stored buyer data.
- `PhoneMaskDirective`, `TicketbookService`, and `CacheKeys` added to the component.

## Template & styles

- `ticketbookNumber` input now binds `(onBlur)="onTicketbookNumberBlur()"`.
- Ticket rows rendered via `@for` with `formArrayName`/`formGroupName` directives; section is hidden until rows exist.
- Added `.ticket-row` / `.ticket-number-label` / `.ticket-field` SCSS rules with responsive stacking.

Assistant: # OctoAcme Project Management Process Summary

OctoAcme follows a structured, lifecycle-based approach to project management that emphasizes customer value, iterative delivery, and clear ownership. The methodology is organized into five key phases: **Initiation**, **Planning**, **Execution**, **Release**, and **Close & Retrospective**. During initiation, teams validate business needs and create a lightweight Project One-pager that defines the problem statement, goals, success metrics, stakeholders, and initial timeline. Once approved by stakeholders and the Product Lead, the project moves into planning, where work is broken into shippable increments with prioritized backlogs, acceptance criteria, and defined milestones. This structured approach ensures alignment before any execution begins and reduces the risk of building the wrong solution.

The execution phase emphasizes iterative delivery through regular team rhythms: daily standups (15 minutes), weekly delivery syncs, and sprint-based planning with small pull requests (≤400 lines). OctoAcme maintains a project board with standardized columns (Backlog, Ready, In Progress, In Review, QA, Done) to provide transparency and enable quick identification of blockers. Quality and testing are embedded throughout execution, requiring unit tests for new logic, integration tests where applicable, end-to-end smoke tests before release, and security scanning in CI. A three-level escalation framework (team triage → PM escalation → sponsor-level escalation) ensures blockers are surfaced and resolved quickly, supported by weekly risk register reviews.

OctoAcme defines clear roles and responsibilities: **Project Managers** coordinate schedules, risks, and communications; **Product Managers** define outcomes and prioritize the backlog; **Developers** implement features and maintain code quality; and **QA/Testing** validates acceptance criteria. Communication happens through weekly syncs between PM and Product Manager, twice-weekly standups, monthly stakeholder updates, and ad-hoc escalations. A single source of truth (project README or release doc) maintains transparency across all stakeholders. Release management is standardized with pre-deployment checklists, staging validation, rollback playbooks, and post-deploy verification, followed by comprehensive release notes. Finally, retrospectives are held after each sprint or milestone to capture learnings, with action items tracked in the backlog and reviewed in weekly PM syncs, creating a continuous improvement culture that feeds validated improvements back into project processes.

author: sunrisepeak
body:
## Summary

- Add Python 3.12.13 (cpython-standalone) download URL for Linux x86_64, enabling `xlings install python@3.12`
- In `config()`, automatically copy `include/` headers into subos sysroot (`subos_sysrootdir()/usr/include/`) so that the subos GCC can find `pyconfig.h` when compiling C extensions
- Multi-version support: both python3.12 and python3.13 headers coexist in sysroot
- Switch versions via `xlings use python@3.12` / `xlings use python@3.13`

## Motivation

When using xlings' subos GCC to `pip install` packages with C extensions (e.g. `evdev`, `mujoco`, `dm-tree`), compilation fails with:

```
fatal error: x86_64-linux-gnu/python3.12/pyconfig.h: No such file or directory
```

The subos GCC only searches `<sysroot>/usr/include/`, which lacks Python dev headers. This PR copies them from the python-build-standalone install into the sysroot during `config()`.

Python 3.12 is also needed for projects like OpenPI which pin `numpy<2.0.0` (incompatible with Python 3.13's dm-tree wheels).

## Test plan

- [x] `xlings install python@3.12 -y` — downloads and installs successfully
- [x] `xlings install python@3.13 -y` — still works
- [x] `xlings use python@3.12` — switches active version
- [x] Both `python3.12/pyconfig.h` and `python3.13/pyconfig.h` present in subos sysroot
- [x] subos GCC can compile `#include <python3.12/pyconfig.h>` successfully
- [x] OpenPI full dependency install succeeds with Python 3.12 venv

author: lee101
body:
## Summary
- Implement TTT evaluation framework in `evaluate_ttt.py` at repo root
- For each holdout window: warm up N steps → mini PPO update of last layers only → continue with adapted policy → restore weights before next window
- Also implements meta checkpoint selection: probe all checkpoints for `selection_steps`, pick the one with highest cumulative reward, run full window with the winner
- Compare TTT vs baseline with side-by-side table output (JSON + human-readable)

## Key design decisions
- Only update actor head + last encoder layer during TTT — prevents catastrophic forgetting of the feature extractor
- KL penalty (`kl_coef=0.1`) bounds how far the adapted policy can drift from the base
- Weights are always restored after each window (TTT is per-window, not cumulative)
- Inference helpers (`_infer_arch`, `_infer_hidden_size`, `_infer_resmlp_blocks`) imported from `pufferlib_market.evaluate_fast` rather than duplicated

## Test plan
- [x] 17 tests in `tests/test_evaluate_ttt.py` (existing LoRA/TTT tests) — all pass
- [x] 17 tests in `tests/test_root_evaluate_ttt.py` (new: `_get_ttt_params`, `_do_ttt_update`, `_load_policy`, weight restoration, comparison table)
- [x] E2E: `python evaluate_ttt.py --checkpoint ... --data-path ... --n-windows 3 --eval-steps 45 --ttt-warmup-steps 10 --verbose` runs end-to-end
- [x] `--help` works correctly with both flat and subcommand CLI forms

author: csummers-dev
body:
- Fixes save corruption caused by incorrect checksum length for item sector (section id=13)
- Changed UNBOUND_ITEM_FIXED_LEN from 0x454 to 0x450 in both frontend and backend

The editor was computing the item sector checksum over 0x454 bytes (1108), but the game expects 0x450 bytes (1104). The extra 4 bytes (at offset 0x450–0x453) can contain non-zero data depending on save state.

When those bytes were zero, which happened to be the case on some saves, the wrong length still produced the correct checksum by coincidence (since adding zero doesn't change a sum). When those bytes were non-zero, the editor wrote an incorrect checksum and the game rejected the save as corrupted. :(

This showed up in saves that used Unbound Cloud trading or had been previously edited. Those things didn't cause the issue, but changes in save data and section rotation left non-zero bytes at that offset, exposing the bug

author: segin
body:
💡 **What:**
Optimized the `ChainedStream` constructor by changing its signature to accept the `paths` argument by `const std::vector<TagLib::String>&` instead of by value and `std::move`. 

🎯 **Why:**
When the caller passes an lvalue (as happens in `src/player.cpp` with `request.paths`), passing by value forces an immediate copy at the call site, which is then moved into the member variable. While passing by value is a common idiom for sink arguments, in scenarios where the argument is predominantly an lvalue and not meant to be consumed by the caller, passing by const reference can be slightly more performant by avoiding the intermediate argument copy and move semantics, directly invoking the copy constructor of the member variable.

📊 **Measured Improvement:**
A focused C++ micro-benchmark was created to simulate the `ChainedStream` initialization with a large number of paths (100 mock `TagLib::String` objects, 10,000 iterations).

**Benchmark Results:**
- Baseline (pass by value + move): ~9.09 ms
- Optimized (pass by const ref): ~7.93 ms
- **Improvement:** ~12.78% reduction in initialization overhead in the measured hot path.

*Note: The actual performance impact will scale with the number of paths provided to the stream.*

author: felictycf
body:
## Summary
- register CSV and TSV document types in the macOS app bundle
- handle Finder/LaunchServices file-open requests on native startup
- add regression coverage for bundle metadata and startup file path handling

## Problem
QuickCSV could be launched manually, but macOS did not recognize it as a CSV/TSV document handler. That meant:
- QuickCSV did not appear reliably in Finder's `Open With` / default app selection for CSV files
- double-clicking a CSV file or using `open -a QuickCSV file.csv` did not route the file into the app's existing load flow

## Implementation details
### 1. Bundle document type registration
Added a dedicated plist fragment at `macos/file-associations.plist` and wired it into `cargo-bundle` via `osx_info_plist_exts`.

The generated `Info.plist` now declares `CFBundleDocumentTypes` for:
- `.csv`
- `.tsv`

### 2. Native file-open handling
Added native startup/open-path plumbing in `src/main.rs` so file paths can be queued before the UI is fully running and then consumed by the app.

On macOS specifically, this PR augments the existing `winit` application delegate class with:
- `application:openFile:`
- `application:openFiles:`
- `application:openURLs:`

That approach is important because replacing `winit`'s delegate causes `winit` to panic on macOS. Extending the registered delegate keeps `winit` in control while still allowing QuickCSV to receive Finder open-document events.

### 3. Open behavior inside the app
Unified native file opening through `open_native_path(...)` so these entry points behave consistently:
- Finder/LaunchServices open-document events
- startup args
- native file dialog
- drag and drop
- recent files reopening

If the app only has the initial empty tab, the first opened file reuses it. Additional files open in new tabs.

## Tests and verification
Automated verification:
- `cargo test`
- `cargo fmt --check`
- regression tests for plist configuration and native startup path handling

Manual/native verification:
- `cargo bundle --release`
- verified generated `QuickCSV.app` contains `CFBundleDocumentTypes`
- verified:
  `open -n -a target/release/bundle/osx/QuickCSV.app /tmp/quickcsv_open_test.csv`
  opens the file and records it in QuickCSV's recent files state

## Notes
This PR is intentionally focused on macOS document association/open flow only.

<!-- This is an auto-generated description by cubic. -->
---
## Summary by cubic
Adds macOS CSV/TSV file associations and handles Finder open events so double‑click and `open -a` route files into QuickCSV’s normal load flow. Queues files during native startup and opens them once the UI is ready; adds tests to prevent regressions.

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Register CSV/TSV document types via `macos/file-associations.plist` + `osx_info_plist_exts`.
  - Extend the `winit` app delegate to handle `application:openFile:`, `application:openFiles:`, and `application:openURLs:` without replacing the delegate; install hooks on startup.

  - Unify native open behavior; reuse the initial empty tab for the first file, then open new tabs (Finder, `open -a`, drag‑and‑drop, args, dialog, recent files).

## Summary

Fix Issue #164: GraphQL Playground 在生产环境暴露内部 API 结构

## Changes

- Set `playground` to `false` when `NODE_ENV` is `production`

In production environments, enabling GraphQL Playground and introspection exposes:

- Potential field permission vulnerabilities

body:
This PR fixes a bug in `index.html` that caused the page to crash with `Uncaught ReferenceError: liveblocks is not defined`.

The issue originated from attempting to load an unavailable UMD build (`https://unpkg.com/@liveblocks/client@0.17.9/dist/liveblocks.umd.js`) via a `<script>` tag. The `@liveblocks/client` package does not appear to provide a UMD build in this or surrounding versions.

To fix this:
1. Replaced the standard `<script>` with `<script type="module">`.
2. Replaced the `unpkg.com` script tag with an ES module import from `esm.sh` for `@liveblocks/client@1.0.0`.
3. Updated the `liveblocks.createClient` call to `createClient` from the import.
4. Exposed UI-bound functions (like `toggleLayer`, `setView`, etc.) to the global `window` object since `<script type="module">` scopes them locally and breaks inline HTML handlers like `onclick="toggleLayer(this)"`.
5. Fixed a secondary crash related to MapLibre's missing `map.setFog` by wrapping it in an `if(map.setFog)` check.
