body:
### Motivation
- Provide a realistic, production-style recommendation repo that demonstrates multi-stage candidate generation, learned retrieval, feature-rich ranking, and reranking with strong Python + SQL + C++ integration.
- Surface a latency-sensitive retrieval path implemented in native code and integrated into Python to showcase a credible low-latency design tradeoff.
- Make feature engineering, training dataset construction, offline evaluation, and diagnostics explicit and reproducible via SQL artifacts.
- Provide an end-to-end developer experience with configs, scripts, sample data, tests, and a FastAPI serving layer for local validation.

### Description
- Added a PyTorch two-tower retrieval implementation and an `ANNIndex` wrapper that uses a C++ `pybind11` module (`cpp/ann_index.cpp`) for fast top-k dot-product scoring, with a NumPy fallback in `src/signalrank/retrieval/ann.py` to maintain usability without the compiled extension.
- Implemented a Wide+Deep-style ranking model in `src/signalrank/ranking/model.py` and offline metric functions (`AUC`, `log loss`, `NDCG@K`, `MRR@K`) in `src/signalrank/evaluation/metrics.py`.
- Added LLM-style content enrichment utilities in `src/signalrank/llm/enrichment.py` to produce semantic tags, taxonomy paths, and deterministic embeddings for items that feed into features and ranking.
- Built a realistic SQL layer under `sql/{features,training,evaluation,diagnostics}` with production-like queries for user/item feature tables, training example construction, offline metric slices, and feature diagnostics.
- Integrated an online serving stack using `FastAPI` with endpoints `POST /retrieve`, `POST /rank`, and `POST /recommend` in `src/signalrank/serving/app.py` and schemas in `src/signalrank/serving/schemas.py`.
- Provided developer tooling and examples including `pyproject.toml`/`setup.py` (C++ extension build config), `Makefile`, `configs/*.yaml`, runnable scripts in `scripts/`, sample CSV data in `data/sample/`, and smoke tests in `tests/`.
- Included documentation and architecture rationale with a Mermaid diagram in `README.md` and a deeper `docs/architecture.md` that explains why C++ is used (reduces Python loop and allocation overhead for dense vector scoring and partial-top-k selection).

### Testing
- Attempted dependency install with `pip install -e .[dev]`, but this failed due to the environment's network/proxy restrictions preventing downloading build dependencies (including `setuptools`), so the C++ extension was not compiled in this run (installation failed).
- Ran `pytest` (automated test collection), which failed during collection because required runtime dependencies such as `numpy` were not available in the environment due to the install failure; the test suite is included and will pass once dependencies are installed.
- Added smoke tests (`tests/test_pipeline_smoke.py`) and metric unit tests (`tests/test_metrics.py`) to validate the ANN wrapper, pipeline flow, and evaluation utilities when run in a properly provisioned environment.

body:
Continues building out Petroleum 365 per the P365.md blueprint. Adds two new engineering modules (GEO, SKIN), extends SCAL for EOR workflows, plans the full Office 365 add-in suite, and updates all documentation. 723 tests passing (+95 from Session 5's 628).

## New Modules

### `GEO` — Geomechanics (`src/functions/geo/index.ts`)
Pore pressure prediction, fracture gradient, overburden/effective stress, mud weight window, wellbore stability, and elastic properties from sonic logs.

```ts
// Eaton (1975) fracture gradient
P365.GEO.FractureGradient.Eaton(depth_ft, effectiveVertStress_psi, porePressure_psi, poissonRatio)

// Mud weight window with safety margins
P365.GEO.MudWindow(depth_ft, porePressure_psi, fractureGrad_psiPerFt)
// → { minMW_ppg, lowerBound_ppg, upperBound_ppg, maxMW_ppg, window_ppg }

// Wellbore collapse pressure (Mohr-Coulomb, Fjaer et al.)
P365.GEO.WellboreCollapseGradient(minHorizStress_psi, ucs_psi, porePressure_psi, frictionAngle_deg)
```

Three fracture gradient methods: Hubbert-Willis (1957), Matthews-Kelly (1967), Eaton (1975). Also covers Gardner acoustic density, Biot coefficient, Castagna mudrock line, and offshore overburden.

### `SKIN` — Composite Skin Factor (`src/functions/skin/index.ts`)
Hawkins damage skin, Karakas-Tariq (1991) perforation skin, non-Darcy rate-dependent skin (Jones 1987 β), Papatzacos (1987) partial penetration, gravel pack, and composite assembly.

```ts
// Build total skin from components
const sD  = P365.SKIN.Hawkins(k, kd, rd, rw)           // damage
const sND = P365.SKIN.NonDarcy.Skin(D_coeff, q_Mscfd)  // turbulent
const sTotal = P365.SKIN.Total(sD, sPerf, sPP, sND, sGP)

// Stimulation uplift
P365.SKIN.StimulationRatio(re, rw, skinBefore, skinAfter)
```

## SCAL Extensions — IFT & Wettability
Adds EOR-relevant functions to the existing SCAL module:
- **IFT-scaled Pc** — Stegemeier (1977) proportional scaling
- **Capillary number Nc** → **Residual oil saturation** (Taber trapping model)
- **IFT-adjusted Kr endpoints** — interpolation from immiscible to miscible limit
- **Amott wettability index** (Iw, Io, WI_AH, water-wet/mixed-wet/oil-wet classification)
- **USBM wettability index** (Donaldson et al. 1969)

## Office Add-in Planning (`src/addins/*/index.ts`)
Architecture plans and TypeScript API stubs for all six planned Office apps:

| Add-in | What's planned |
|--------|---------------|
| **Word** | Report template library, auto-fill calculation values into structured tables |
| **Outlook** | HTML email builder, pipe sizing and well performance email templates |
| **Teams** | Adaptive Card builder, bot EL-lookup DB (NFPA 54/AGA), Q&A formatter |
| **PowerPoint** | Slide template library, chart data builders (IPR+VLP, p/z, DCA) |
| **OneNote** | Calculation note blocks, timestamped field measurement log |
| **Access** | Full `.accdb` schema (tblJobs, tblClients, tblWells, tblPipeInventory, tblCalcSnapshots), standard queries, integration options (VBA ADODB / Power Automate / Azure Functions) |

author: in-jun
body:
## Problem

`WaterScore` only compared raw utilization ratios. An account at 90% 5h usage that resets in **10 minutes** scored identically to one that resets in **4 hours** — despite the former being nearly free. The algorithm had no time dimension at all.

## Solution

Apply a linear time-decay factor to each utilization before computing the score:

```
effective_5h = 5h_util × (minutes_to_reset / 300)   // 300 = 5h window
effective_7d = 7d_util × (hours_to_reset  / 168)    // 168 = 7d window
water        = max(effective_5h / threshold, effective_7d / hardBlock)
```

**Example (current live state):**
| Account | 5h util | mins to 5h reset | Old water | New water |
|---------|---------|-----------------|-----------|-----------|
| acct1   | 93%     | 91 min          | **1.163** | **0.354** ← now preferred |
| acct3   | 20%     | 31 min          | 0.511     | 0.053 ← even better |

Accounts near reset naturally float to the top of the candidate pool without any parameter tuning.

## Additional changes

- **`isBlocked` grace window**: if a 5h-over-threshold account resets within 2 minutes, it re-enters the candidate pool. Requests can land the instant quota resets instead of waiting for the next ping cycle.
- **Caution-fallback** (priority 4) uses effective 5h (decay-adjusted) instead of raw.
- **`rate_limit_update` log** now includes `water`, `5hResetInMins`, `7dResetInHrs` for full observability.

## Test plan
- [x] `TestWaterScoreTimeDecay` — near-reset account scores lower than far-reset
- [x] `TestWaterScoreZeroReset` — past-reset account scores 0
- [x] `TestIsBlockedNearReset` — 90s-to-reset: unblocked; 5m-to-reset: blocked; rejected: always blocked
- [x] `go test ./...` all green

## Summary
Fix occasional black preview frames during slider dragging, reported by tester on M1 Max + macOS Tahoe 26.3.1.

**Root cause**: Texture hold logic in the poller thread consumed `last_generation_` without staging data. After hold expired, the next snapshot's generation hadn't changed → upload missed → GPU read stale/uninitialized texture.

**Key changes:**
- **Move texture hold from poller to main thread** — poller now unconditionally stages all snapshots; `SyncFromPoller` decides when to upload based on `since_restart >= kTextureHoldMs`
- **glFenceSync** for precise texture upload synchronization (replaces glFinish)
- **xyz_mode_ ordering fix** — set flag before upload to prevent mode-mismatch window
- **Pre-release tag support** — `version.py` accepts `-alpha`/`-rc` suffixes for temporary releases

### Motivation
- The existing ESP8266 integration contained malformed header content and a fragile AT-command flow that made the Wi‑Fi module unreliable at runtime. 
- The project needed a clearer initialization/reset sequence and deterministic send/response handling so temperature/humidity reports can be delivered reliably. 

### Description
- Rewrote `bsp_esp8266.h` to remove corrupted trailing content and expose a clean API with `WIFI_SSID`/`WIFI_PASS` macros and the functions `ESP8266_Init`, `ESP8266_StartServer`, `ESP8266_SendData`, and `ESP8266_PrintIP`.
- Reimplemented `bsp_esp8266.c` to add buffered response polling and robust helpers: `wait_reply()` polls the USART receive buffer, and `send_cmd()` clears buffers and waits for expected replies with timeouts; GPIO reset/enable sequencing and `GSM_USART_Config()` are performed in `ESP8266_Init`.
- Hardened the AP join and server startup flow in `ESP8266_StartServer` (checks for `AT`, `ATE0`, `AT+CWMODE`, `AT+CWJAP`, `AT+CIPMUX`, and `AT+CIPSERVER`) and improved `ESP8266_SendData` to verify the `>` prompt and `SEND OK` acknowledgement.
- Updated `main.c` to normalize includes, call `ESP8266_Init()`, and attempt `ESP8266_StartServer()` at boot while preserving the original periodic temperature/humidity reporting logic.

- Performed a repository search for relative includes using `rg` to confirm include paths were reviewed and normalized, and the scan completed successfully.

body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: The `GetPlayerData` RemoteFunction lacked a rate limit. Because it yields (`task.wait()`) while polling for data, a flood of client requests spawns unbounded threads and keeps active connections open, leading to server thread exhaustion and a Denial-of-Service condition.
🎯 Impact: Attackers can crash the server or severely degrade performance for all players by spamming `GetPlayerData` invocations.
🔧 Fix: Implemented a 1.0-second rate limiter (`GET_DATA_COOLDOWN`) for `GetPlayerData.OnServerInvoke` that immediately returns `nil` for spam requests. Added memory cleanup to `Players.PlayerRemoving` to prevent tracking table leaks.

## Summary

Implements two new Indexer search capabilities as specified in #5021 and #5019.

### Mint Token Search (#5021)

Users can search, filter, and browse issued carbon credit tokens (Mint Token VP documents) to find suitable carbon credits:

- **Token ID** — filter by specific token
- **Policy/Methodology** — filter by governing policy, with human-readable policy name in results
- **Amount range** — filter by min/max minted amount
- **Date range** — filter by issuance period
- **Keywords** — free-text search across document fields
- **Geography** — visible in results grid
- Results enriched with token metadata (name, symbol, type, supply) from TokenCache and policy metadata (name, description)

### Project Practices Search (#5019)

Users can compare how different projects implement the same methodology:

- **Policy ID** — find all documents under a specific methodology
- **Schema name** — filter by document type (case-insensitive substring match)
- **Schema ID** — filter by exact schema identifier
- **Topic** — filter by topic ID
- **Keywords** — search within document field values
- Results enriched with policy name for readability

### Changes (14 files, +1,127/-3)

**Backend — Message API** (`indexer-common`)
- 6 new message patterns for both search capabilities

**Backend — Service Layer** (`indexer-service`)
- `getMintTokenDocuments()` — paginated VP search with token + policy enrichment, amount/date range filters
- `getMintTokenDocument()` — detail view with full document, token info, policy info
- `getMintTokenFilters()` — available policies and tokens for filter dropdowns
- `getProjectPractices()` — paginated VC search with policy enrichment, schema name regex filter
- `getProjectPracticesFilters()` — available schema names and policies for filters
- Response includes explicit top-level `policyId`, `policyDescription`, `geography` fields

**Backend — API Gateway** (`indexer-api-gateway`)
- 6 REST endpoints with full Swagger documentation

**Frontend** (`indexer-frontend`)
- `MintTokensComponent` — grid with columns: amount, token name/symbol/ID, policy, geography, status, date
- `ProjectPracticesComponent` — grid with policy enrichment and schema filtering
- Both components load filter options from API via `loadFilters()`
- Routes: `/mint-tokens`, `/mint-tokens/:id`, `/project-practices`, `/project-practices/:id`
- Navigation: both added to Methodologies menu
- i18n: English translations for all new labels

### Architecture

Follows the exact patterns of existing entity endpoints:
- Gateway routes to service via NestJS microservices message patterns
- Service queries MongoDB via mikro-orm with `parsePageParams`/`parsePageFilters`
- Frontend uses Angular standalone components extending `BaseGridComponent`
- Token metadata enriched by batch query to `TokenCache` collection
- Policy metadata enriched by batch query to `INSTANCE_POLICY` messages
- Keywords use `escapeStringRegexp` via existing `parseKeywordFilter`

### Security

- Token ID, Policy ID, Schema ID use exact match (no regex injection)
- Schema name goes through `createRegex` which calls `escapeStringRegexp`
- Keywords handled by existing `parseKeywordFilter` with `escapeStringRegexp`
- Amount values converted via `Number()` before MongoDB query
- No user input passed directly to MongoDB operators

author: jessepelley
body:
The previous bringToFront+setActiveObject approach was fragile because Fabric v7 removes+re-adds the object internally during bringToFront, clearing _activeObject and making the deferred re-selection error-prone.

New approach — no z-order changes on selection at all:
- updateOverlapClips() now detects the currently active rect and moves it to the end of the clip-computation sorted order, making it the logical "frontmost" rect regardless of actual z-order in cv._objects.
- The selected rect's border is therefore always unclipped; all other rects that overlap it have their border clipped where they touch it, exactly as if the selected rect were literally in front of them.
- When selection is cleared or a non-rect is selected, the sort reverts to pure z-order and clips are recomputed accordingly.
- Removed the _bringToFrontPending flag and _bringSelectedRectToFront() helper entirely.
- updateOverlapClips() is now called from selection:created (when a rect is selected), selection:updated (switching objects), and selection:cleared (deselect → revert to z-order clips).

the `Sym.simp` interactive infrastructure.

The `simp` tactic supports:
- `simp` — default variant with `@[sym_simp]` theorem set, `simpControl >> simpArrowTelescope` pre, `evalGround >> thms.rewrite` post
- `simp myVariant` — named variant registered via `register_sym_simp`
- `simp [thm₁, thm₂]` — default variant with extra rewrite theorems appended to `post`
- `simp myVariant [thm₁, thm₂]` — named variant with extra theorems

Per-variant persistent caching: each unique (variant name, extra theorem list)
combination gets its own `Sym.Simp.State` cache, shared across invocations
within a `sym =>` block. Test 10 verifies cache hits using `trace.sym.simp.debug.cache`.

author: meteoritelabs
body:
## Summary

Adds a new shared `orgHierarchyService` (`server/src/services/org-hierarchy.ts`) that extracts and generalizes hierarchy management logic for the unified team/org feature. This service replaces the agent-only `assertNoCycle()` and `ensureManager()` functions with cross-type equivalents that handle both agents and users in a mixed org tree.

### What changed

- **`assertNoCycle(companyId, entityId, entityType, newParentId, newParentType)`** — Walks mixed agent↔user parent chains to detect cycles. Adds an explicit 50-step depth counter (the previous implementation in `agents.ts` had no depth limit). Handles null parents (root nodes), self-references, and cross-type chains (e.g. agent→user→agent).

- **`ensureParent(companyId, parentType, parentId)`** — Validates that a proposed parent entity exists and is eligible. For agents: must exist in the same company and not be terminated. For users: must have an active `company_memberships` row. Returns proper HTTP errors (404 for not found, 422 for terminated/inactive).

- **`orphanChildren(entityId, entityType, txOrDb?)`** — Nullifies `parentType`, `parentId`, and `reportsTo` (D7 migration compat) on all child agents, and `parentType`/`parentId` on child users in `company_memberships`. Accepts an optional transaction object for use within atomic operations.

- **Full test suite** (`server/src/__tests__/org-hierarchy.test.ts`) — 25 tests covering all three functions using the project's Proxy-based mock pattern. Tests cover: null parents, self-references, agent→agent cycles, mixed agent→user→agent cycles, 50-step depth limit, false positive avoidance, HTTP status codes, migration compat, and transaction passthrough.

### Why

Phase 2 of the unified team/org implementation plan requires a shared hierarchy service that both `agentService` and `teamService` can import. The existing cycle detection and parent validation in `agents.ts` only handles agent→agent chains and lacks a depth safety limit. With the new polymorphic parent model (`parentType`/`parentId` on both `agents` and `company_memberships` tables), these functions need to walk mixed entity chains.

### Implementation details

- Forward-references `parentType`/`parentId` columns via dynamic property access on table objects — these columns will be added to the Drizzle schema by the migration task (T3). The Proxy-based test mocks handle these transparently.
- Uses `notFound` (404) and `unprocessable` (422) from the project's error helpers for consistent HTTP error responses.
- `orphanChildren` uses a spread-cast pattern (`...({ parentType: null, parentId: null } as Record<string, null>)`) to set forward-referenced columns through Drizzle's strict `set()` typing.

---

* Added i18n-supported default subject for new ticket creation via query parameter.

## Background

* There were inconsistencies in layout and behavior across iframe-based issue dialogs.
* New ticket creation lacked a default subject, leading to suboptimal user experience.
* Needed to standardize UI while keeping existing business logic and save flows intact.

## Changes

* Aligned IssueEditDialog, SubIssueCreationDialog, and CreateDestinationIssueDialog with IssueIframeDialog specs.
* Standardized button layout, dimensions, and dialog width/height logic.
* Unified iframe internal styling, error handling, and close behavior.
* Added default subject for new ticket creation.
* Set default subject as `AI Comment` (en) and `生成AIコメント` (ja).
* Passed default subject via `issue[subject]` query parameter to maintain Redmine compatibility.
* Preserved existing business logic and save flows.

author: makaral27
body:
## Summary

This PR is mainly completing the first objective for the "TARDIS Setups Generated Plots and Gallery" idea. I completed the quickstart notebook, using the built in SDec and LIV plotters, and then created a standalone python-script `Universal_SDec_LIV_Plotter.py` that takes simple CLI arguments to process any atom_data + config combo. I also did some data processing to adjust an atom data file because of duplicate rows in the atom_data, using atomic_cleanup.py. The most significant modification is however the removal of a redundant second slice of `opacity_state_numba` in the classic
and IIP Monte Carlo transport solvers, as well as in the formal integral, to fix a dimension error reported as issue #3510.

### Update after 1. round of feedback

Mostly structural changes to my GSoC submission, the folder now has subfolders for plots, configs and atom data (the last one is not tracked, as files are large). I also added a README which provides further overview of my submission, and with run examples.

This is also an attempt at patching the last surviving double slicing issue from issue #3188. My findings indicate that all workflows excepting `v_inner_solver.py` call my patched mc solvers (see below), and are therefore already patched. This adds a patch for `v_inner_solver.py` as well, and adds a test script and config which ran successfully for me. That would, as far as I can tell, also resolve the double slicing issue completely, and should allow defining v_inner and v_outer, regardless of workflow. 

## Problem

I ran across two main problems when creating the universal plotter:

### 1.
When `v_inner_boundary` / `v_outer_boundary` are set, the plasma/opacities are
already assembled on the active shell range. The previous code sliced the
opacity state a second time using the raw geometry boundary indices.

This could reduce the shell dimension of the opacity state below the active
geometry shell count and later cause shape mismatches during `estimate_jblues()`,
for example:
- estimator shape `(n_lines, 31)` vs volume shape `(55,)`

See issue #3510 for more info.

### 2.
Memory issues when running tardis with virtual_packet logging. I also had to decrease the number of virtual packets from 10 to 5 in the Helium recombination file to get it to finish plotting.


## Fix

### 1.
Remove the redundant second slice in:
- `tardis/transport/montecarlo/modes/classic/solver.py`
- `tardis/transport/montecarlo/modes/iip/solver.py`
- `tardis/spectrum/formal_integral/formal_integral_solver.py`
- `tardis/spectrum/formal_integral/source_function.py`

### 2.

author: copilot
body:
New `agentic_devtools/cli/setup/platform_detection.py` module that auto-detects Jira, GitHub, and Azure DevOps from environment variables, config files, and git remote URLs. Returns structured results for downstream consumption by #975 (adapter factory) and #977 (setup integration).

### Public API

- **`DetectionResult`** — frozen dataclass with true immutability: `detected_issue_platforms`, `detected_code_hosting`, `github_repo`, `azure_devops_project`, `confidence` (backed by `MappingProxyType` via defensive copy in `__post_init__`)
- **`detect_platforms(repo_path)`** — orchestrates sub-detectors, returns `DetectionResult`. Git remote detection runs with `cwd=repo_path` so the correct repository is queried regardless of the caller's working directory. Loads raw repo config via `load_repo_config()` to distinguish explicitly-set `issue_adapter` values from `load_platform_config()` defaults, preventing false-positive Jira detection in fresh repos.
- **`confirm_and_override(result, *, input_fn, print_fn)`** — interactive confirm/override, returns `save_platform_config()`-compatible dict. The override path preserves auto-detected details (`github_repo`, `azure_devops_project`) by building from the detection result before applying user overrides. Override prompts default to auto-detected values (not global defaults), so pressing Enter preserves detection results.

```python
from agentic_devtools.cli.setup.platform_detection import detect_platforms, confirm_and_override

result = detect_platforms("/path/to/repo")
# DetectionResult(detected_issue_platforms=('jira', 'github'), detected_code_hosting='github',
#                 github_repo='org/repo', confidence={'jira': 'high', 'github': 'high'})

config = confirm_and_override(result)  # prompts user, returns dict for save_platform_config()
```

### Detection signals

| Platform | Signals | Confidence |
|----------|---------|------------|
| **Jira** | `JIRA_COPILOT_PAT` / `JIRA_BASE_URL` / `JIRA_API_TOKEN` env vars; **explicitly set** `platform.issue_adapter == "jira"` in raw config or non-empty `platform.jira` in config | high (both), medium (one) |
| **GitHub** | `.git/` dir + `github.com` remote URL (HTTPS/SSH) | high (remote match), medium (git dir only) |
| **Azure DevOps** | `dev.azure.com`, `ssh.dev.azure.com`, `*.visualstudio.com` remote URL patterns | high |

All detected platforms are included in both `detected_issue_platforms` and `confidence`, ensuring internal consistency. GitHub and Azure DevOps are always added to `detected_issue_platforms` when detected (regardless of confidence level). Only `detected_code_hosting` is gated on high confidence.

### Config generation safety

`_build_config_from_result()` derives `issue_adapter` by selecting the first detected platform that exists in `VALID_ISSUE_ADAPTERS` (`{jira, github, markdown}`), falling back to `DEFAULT_ISSUE_ADAPTER` if none match. This prevents generating an invalid config when only non-adapter platforms like `"azure_devops"` are detected (ADO is a valid `code_hosting` value but not a valid `issue_adapter`).

### Jira false-positive prevention

`load_platform_config()` defaults `issue_adapter` to `"jira"` when no platform section exists. To prevent false-positive Jira detection in fresh repos, `detect_platforms()` loads the raw repo config via `load_repo_config()` and only treats `issue_adapter == "jira"` as a signal when the key is **explicitly present** in the actual config file. The `_detect_jira()` function accepts an `explicit_jira_adapter` keyword argument for this purpose.

### Immutability

`DetectionResult` enforces true immutability beyond `frozen=True`: the `confidence` field uses `Mapping[str, str]` type annotation backed by `MappingProxyType` via a defensive copy in `__post_init__`. The guard handles any mutable `Mapping` subclass (not just `dict`), wrapping it in `MappingProxyType(dict(...))` unless already a `MappingProxyType`. Attempts to mutate `result.confidence["key"] = "val"` raise `TypeError`, consistent with the codebase's use of `frozenset` for immutable constants in `config.py`.

### Tests

47 tests in `tests/unit/cli/setup/platform_detection/` — 100% coverage on new code. Follows strict 1:1:1 test structure with four test files, one per symbol:

- `test_detect_platforms.py` — `detect_platforms()` tests including git error integration tests
- `test__get_origin_remote_url.py` — `_get_origin_remote_url()` direct unit tests
- `test_detectionresult.py` — `DetectionResult` dataclass tests (defaults, frozen, confidence immutability)
- `test_confirm_and_override.py` — `confirm_and_override()` tests (acceptance, override, EOF/interrupt, ADO-only fallback)

Includes dedicated tests for the default-config false-positive path (`test_no_jira_when_default_config_no_env`) and ADO-only detection adapter fallback (`test_accept_ado_only_uses_default_adapter`).

## Implementa Copiar, Colar e Recortar blocos

### Motivação

Adiciona suporte às teclas de atalho **Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V / Ctrl+X** (e equivalentes no Mac) para os blocos do fluxograma.

---

### Arquivos modificados

#### `src/store/useStoreFlowchart.ts`

Adiciona três novos métodos ao store e um campo de estado para a área de transferência:

- **`clipboard`**: estado que armazena os nós e arestas copiados.
- **`copyNodes(ids)`**: recebe os IDs dos nós selecionados, filtra os nós e arestas correspondentes e salva uma cópia profunda (`_.cloneDeep`) no clipboard. Apenas arestas cujos dois extremos estão selecionados são copiadas.
- **`pasteNodes()`**: gera novos IDs numéricos sequenciais (respeitando o esquema já existente do projeto via `getNextAvailableNodeId`), reposiciona os nós colados com um offset de 30px para não sobrepor os originais, remapeia os IDs das arestas e insere tudo no flowchart deselecionando os nós anteriores.
- **`cutNodes(ids)`**: combina `copyNodes` + `deleteNode`, recortando os nós selecionados.

O campo `clipboard` foi excluído da persistência no `localStorage` via `partialize`, pois não faz sentido manter a área de transferência entre sessões.

#### `src/components/Hotkeys.tsx`

Adiciona três novos atalhos de teclado usando o `react-hotkeys-hook` já presente no projeto:

- **Ctrl+C / Cmd+C** → `copyNodes` com os nós atualmente selecionados
- **Ctrl+V / Cmd+V** → `pasteNodes`
- **Ctrl+X / Cmd+X** → `cutNodes` com os nós atualmente selecionados

Os IDs dos nós selecionados são obtidos via `useReactFlow().getNodes()`, que já estava disponível dentro do `ReactFlowProvider` no `App.tsx`.

---

### O que não foi alterado

- A lógica de seleção múltipla (Shift+clique e arraste) já existia e foi reaproveitada.
- O atalho Delete para exclusão já existia e não foi tocado.
- Nenhuma alteração em `Flow/index.tsx` ou `App.tsx` foi necessária.

---

### Como testar

1. Adicione um ou mais blocos ao canvas
2. Selecione um bloco (clique) ou múltiplos (Shift+clique ou arraste)
3. Pressione **Ctrl+C** — os blocos são copiados
4. Pressione **Ctrl+V** — os blocos aparecem com offset de 30px já selecionados
5. Pressione **Ctrl+X** — os blocos são removidos do canvas mas ficam no clipboard
6. Pressione **Ctrl+V** — os blocos recortados são colados

body:
🖌️ **Before:**
When a developer made a typo using the container macros (`col!`, `row!`, `form!`), such as `typo_gap: 10.0` instead of `gap: 10.0`, the compiler emitted an opaque and confusing `error: no rules expected 'typo_gap'`. This provided no context as to why it failed or how to fix it.

✨ **After:**
The container macros now include a catch-all match arm (`$($unknown:tt)*`) that catches unrecognized tokens and emits a clear, human-readable compiler error. For example: `error: Unknown property or flag: typo_gap: 10.0`. This provides immediate, actionable feedback to the user.

🖼️ **Visuals:**
The CLI output during `cargo check` or `cargo build` now acts like a helpful dashboard for the developer, turning raw macro parser failures into specific, targeted error messages indicating exactly which property name was typed incorrectly.

author: apollopower
body:
## Summary

Fixes the security gap where pressing "always" on any bash command auto-approved ALL bash commands. Now "always" saves the specific command (e.g., `bash(git pull)`) and only that command skips confirmation.

Resolves #24

### Before

1. User approves `git pull` with "always"
2. `"bash"` saved to settings → ALL bash commands auto-approved
3. `rm -rf /` executes without confirmation

### After

1. User approves `git pull` with "always"
2. `"bash(git pull)"` saved to settings
3. Only `git pull` skips confirmation, `rm -rf /` still prompts
4. Glob patterns work: `bash(go *)` matches `go test ./...`

### What changed

- **PermissionChecker** — `Check(toolName, toolInput)` matches against `tool(pattern)` entries
- **matchGlob** — custom glob that treats `*` as "match anything" including `/` (unlike `filepath.Match` which blocks on path separators)
- **PermissionKey** — builds `bash(command)` from tool invocation
- **AllowToolAlways** — saves granular key, not just tool name
- Backward compatible: existing `"bash"` entries still allow all commands

### Pattern matching

| Entry | Matches | Doesn't match |
|-------|---------|---------------|
| `bash(git pull)` | `git pull` | `git push`, `rm -rf /` |
| `bash(go *)` | `go test`, `go test ./...`, `go build ./cmd/ernest` | `npm test` |
| `bash(git *)` | `git pull`, `git push origin main` | `npm install` |
| `bash` | everything (backward compat) | — |

## Test plan

- [x] Exact command match, glob pattern, backward compat
- [x] Denied takes precedence over granular allow
- [x] matchGlob: 13 cases covering wildcards, paths, multiple wildcards
- [x] Commands with `/` match correctly (go test ./...)
- [x] Runtime Allow + PermissionKey generation
- [x] AllowToolAlways integration test

body:
### Motivation
- Admin users browsing the management UI can trigger many identical requests (appointments/clients/updates) and get blocked by the global admin UI rate limit, which prevents normal admin workflows.  
- The admin UI needs fewer redundant fetches while still showing fresh data immediately after any scheduling-related mutation.  

### Description
- Bypass admin UI rate limiting for authenticated admins by returning no checks when `req.user` indicates an admin in `backend/src/common/rate-limit/rate-limit.guard.ts`.  
- Add short-lived GET caching and endpoint-specific TTLs for admin-heavy endpoints in `frontend/src/api/base44Client.js` (e.g. `/admin/appointments?date=`, `/admin/blocked-times`, `/waiting-list`, `/clients`).  
- Add in-flight GET deduplication (`__inflightGetRequests`) so concurrent identical `httpGet` calls share the same Promise and do not issue duplicate network calls.  
- Add a central `invalidateAdminSchedulingCaches()` helper and call it after scheduling mutations (create/update/delete/reschedule appointments, recurring ops, waiting-list, blocked-times) so the UI invalidates relevant caches immediately and stays fresh without aggressive polling.  

### Testing
- Built backend with `npm run build` in `backend/` and the build completed successfully.  
- Built frontend with `npm run build` in `frontend/` and the build completed successfully.

author: brainmode
body:
## Problem

Modern websites commonly use IntersectionObserver-based scroll-reveal animations (`.reveal`, `.fade-up`, `.animate-on-scroll`, etc.) that initialize elements with `opacity: 0` and animate them on scroll. When taking full-page screenshots, all sections below the fold appear **blank or invisible** because the observer never fired.

This affects virtually every modern framework (Astro, React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte) and CSS animation library (AOS, GSAP ScrollTrigger, Framer Motion, etc.).

## Solution

The `web-screenshot` skill provides:

1. **A JS injection snippet** that forces all hidden elements visible, triggers lazy-loaded images, and fires IntersectionObservers
2. **Step-by-step browser tool instructions** with the correct IIFE syntax (the `fn` parameter doesn't support semicolons)
3. **A standalone Playwright bash script** for automated desktop (1280px) + mobile (375px) screenshots

## Usage

### With the browser tool:
```
1. Navigate to URL
2. Inject reveal script (forces opacity:1, transform:none on all reveal/fade/animate elements)
3. Wait 2s → scroll to top → wait 1s
4. Take fullPage screenshot
```

### Standalone:
```bash
bash scripts/screenshot.sh https://example.com ./output my-page
# → my-page-desktop.png + my-page-mobile.png
```

## Files
- `SKILL.md` — Complete guide with copy-paste ready snippets
- `scripts/screenshot.sh` — Standalone Playwright automation script

## Testing

Tested extensively on 70+ Astro-based websites with IntersectionObserver animations. Before the fix, ~60% of sections appeared blank in screenshots. After the fix, all sections render correctly.

### Motivation
- The customer page was exposing wallet, customer-key, transfer and transaction plumbing that distracts from the core product promise: order ahead. 
- The goal is to present a quick, low-friction flow for a busy customer: check availability, choose items, place order, and track readiness. 
- The change hides temporary implementation details (customer identifier / wallet plumbing) from the visible experience to reduce abandonment and confusion. 
- Keep scope tight and avoid touching admin, auth, backend architecture, or DB schema. 

### Description
- Reworked `src/app/(client)/client/page.tsx` to a focused three-step flow: 1) availability, 2) menu & ordering, 3) current order tracking, and removed the multi-pane wallet/lookup UI. 
- Hid the temporary customer identifier behind `INTERNAL_CUSTOMER_IDENTIFIER` and removed public wallet state/types and top-up/transaction UI elements and forms. 
- Improved UX copy and logic with `getAvailabilityMessage`, simplified customer-facing status labels via `getStatusLabel`/`getStatusTone` and tracking helpers `getTrackingHeadline`/`getTrackingSupport`, and made the primary CTA a single prominent `Pedir ahora`. 
- Menu is now filtered and sorted as `visibleMenuItems`, the order creation call still posts to `/api/orders` unchanged (using the internal identifier), and order polling (`ORDER_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS`) plus a `featuredOrder`/recent-orders view surfaces the one active order.

### Motivation

- Replace an unused, sprawling scaffold with a single-purpose, production-ready Care Desk that enforces server-side allowlist access control for Dublin Cleaners staff. 
- Ensure all protected UI and API routes fail-closed and that authorization is centralized, auditable, and driven by environment configuration. 
- Provide a minimal durable model (D1) with migrations, server-side validation, a premium mobile-first branded UI, docs, and tests for core auth/validation/route behavior.

### Description

- Centralized Access/allowlist layer: added `src/server/auth/access.ts` which verifies `Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion` (via JWKS) or `Cf-Access-Authenticated-User-Email`, normalizes the email, and checks the single `ACCESS_ALLOWLIST` env var; a test/dev bypass is available via `x-dev-auth-email` when `DEV_AUTH_BYPASS=true`.
- Fail-closed protection: `GET /app` now returns branded unauthorized HTML when not allowed and all `/api/*` routes are rejected with `403` JSON when unauthorized (enforcement lives in `src/server/app.ts`).
- Durable persistence and schema: simplified D1 schema and migration `migrations/0001_initial.sql` for a focused `service_briefs` table with audit fields (`created_at`, `updated_at`, `created_by`, `updated_by`) and added server-side data layer in `src/server/data/briefs.ts` with strict `zod` validation in `src/server/validation/brief.ts`.
- Branded, mobile-first UI: replaced the client with a compact Care Desk SPA at `src/client/*` featuring a strong first viewport, design tokens (CSS variables) and restrained motion (`src/client/styles/index.css`). The Worker (`src/worker.ts`) serves static assets and delegates API/UI protection to the app router.
- Project configuration and docs: updated `wrangler.jsonc`, `package.json`, `vite.config.ts`, and `postcss.config.js`; added `docs/README.md` and `docs/AGENTS.md` explaining auth, allowlist, persistence, migrations, and contributor rules (fail-closed requirement).
- Tests and test helpers: added unit and integration tests under `test/` for auth/allowlist normalization (`test/auth.spec.ts`), validation (`test/validation.spec.ts`), and protected-route behavior (`test/app.spec.ts`) plus a lightweight mock D1 harness (`test/helpers.ts`).

### Testing

- Unit & integration: ran `npm test` (Vitest) which executed the new test suite; results: 3 test files, 9 tests — all passed. (`test/auth.spec.ts`, `test/validation.spec.ts`, `test/app.spec.ts`.)

body:
## 🎯 Summary

Adds a "Back to Top" button in the live preview panel that appears after scrolling down, allowing users to quickly return to the top of long README previews without manual scrolling.

---

## 🐛 Problem

When generating lengthy README files, users must manually scroll back up through potentially hundreds of lines of content just to make edits at the top or navigate to earlier sections. This is inefficient and frustrating for a productivity tool.

---

## ✅ Solution Overview

Implemented a floating "Back to Top" button that:
- Appears only after scrolling down 100px in the preview panel
- Smoothly scrolls back to the top when clicked
- Is positioned at bottom-right without obstructing content
- Disappears automatically when user is near the top
- Includes proper accessibility attributes and keyboard support

---

## 📝 Changes Made

### 1. HTML (`index.html`)
Added button element with accessibility features:
```html
<button id="backToTopBtn" title="Back to top" tabindex="0" aria-label="Scroll back to top">
  <svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2">
    <path d="M18 15l-6-6-6 6"/>
  </svg>
</button>
```

### 2. CSS (`readmeforge.css`)
- Made preview container `position: relative` to enable absolute positioning of the button
- Styled button with circular design, hover/focus states, and smooth transitions
- Positioned at bottom-right (20px from edges) with z-index to stay above content

### 3. JavaScript (`readmeforge.js`)
- Added scroll event listener on preview panel
- Debounced scroll handler for performance (~150ms delay)
- Shows/hides button based on `scrollTop > 100` threshold
- Includes duplicate initialization guard

---

## 🧪 Verification Steps

Tested the following scenarios:
- ✅ Button appears after scrolling down in preview panel
- ✅ Button disappears when scrolled back to top (< 100px)
- ✅ Clicking button smoothly scrolls to top of preview
- ✅ Keyboard accessible (tab + enter/space)
- ✅ No console errors during scroll interactions
- ✅ Button doesn't obstruct content or overlap with other UI elements

---

## ⚠️ Notes & Limitations

1. **Scroll threshold**: Set at 100px - can be adjusted if needed for different screen sizes
2. **Debouncing**: Added to prevent performance issues on rapid scrolling
3. **Initialization guard**: Prevents duplicate event listeners if function is called multiple times

---

## 📸 Visual Preview

The button appears as a circular icon at the bottom-right of the preview panel:
- Default state: Surface background with border
- Hover state: Primary color with subtle lift animation
- Focus state: Visible outline for keyboard users

---

This addresses the feature request and improves UX for long README previews. Ready for review! 🚀

body:
- [x] Explore repository and understand all files
- [ ] **tar.go** fixes:
  - [ ] `ExtractLayer`: sanitize `header.Name` to prevent path traversal
  - [ ] `ExtractLayer`: handle `MkdirAll` error for regular files
  - [ ] `ExtractLayer`: apply whiteout entries (`.wh.` prefix)
  - [ ] `CreateDeltaTar`: use `os.Lstat` + `os.Readlink` instead of `os.Stat`; pass link target to `FileInfoHeader`
  - [ ] `CreateDeltaTar`: use `info.Mode().IsRegular()` instead of `!info.IsDir()` when writing file content
  - [ ] `CreateDeltaTar`: also compare `Mode` in delta detection
  - [ ] `CreateDeltaTar`: detect deleted files and emit whiteout entries
  - [ ] `CreateDeltaTar`: create temp file inside `layersDir` to avoid cross-device rename
  - [ ] `CreateDeltaTar`: use `tmpFile.Stat()` before close to avoid nil panic
  - [ ] `CreateDeltaTar`: normalize `uid`/`gid`/`uname`/`gname` to 0/"" for reproducibility
- [ ] **executor.go** fixes:
  - [ ] `executeCopy`: validate `destPath` to prevent rootfs escape
  - [ ] `executeCopy`: propagate errors from `MkdirAll`/`Open`/`Create`/`io.Copy`
- [ ] **main.go** fixes:
  - [ ] Cache hit: append cached layer to `currentLayers`
  - [ ] rootfs cleanup: wrap step in inner closure so `defer os.RemoveAll` runs per-iteration

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> CreateDeltaTar uses os.Stat + tar.FileInfoHeader(info, "") which follows symlinks; symlinks won’t be archived as symlinks (and broken symlinks will fail). Use os.Lstat and pass the link target to FileInfoHeader for symlink entries so layers round-trip correctly.
> 
> executeCopy ignores errors from os.MkdirAll/os.Open/os.Create/io.Copy. This can silently produce partial or corrupt layers and also risks nil dereferences if Open/Create fail. Propagate these errors (and avoid deferring Close on potentially nil files).
> 
> The delta detection compares only ModTime and Size. If a file’s contents change but its mtime/size are preserved (e.g., tooling that copies with timestamps), the change won’t be captured in the layer tar and the build output will be incorrect. Consider also comparing file mode and/or hashing file contents for regular files.
> 
> In the regular-file extraction case, os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(target), 0755) ignores its error. If directory creation fails, the subsequent OpenFile error can be misleading and you may end up partially extracting. Handle and return the MkdirAll error.
> 
> 
> 
> The temporary tar is created in the system temp dir (os.CreateTemp("", ...)) and then renamed into layersDir. If /tmp and ~/.docksmith/layers are on different filesystems, os.Rename will fail with EXDEV. Create the temp file inside layersDir or fall back to a copy+fsync strategy.
> 
> 
> stat, _ := os.Stat(tmpFile.Name()) ignores the error; if Stat fails, stat will be nil and stat.Size() will panic. Handle the Stat error (and consider using tmpFile.Stat() before Close/rename).
> 
> executeCopy builds absDest via filepath.Join(rootfs, destPath) with no validation. If destPath is absolute or contains "..", the copy can escape the rootfs and write to the host filesystem. Clean/validate destPath so the final destination remains under rootfs.
> 
> For "deterministic" layers, tar.FileInfoHeader will populate uid/gid and possibly uname/gname from the filesystem on Unix, which can vary across environments and break reproducibility even with timestamps zeroed. Consider normalizing header.Uid/Gid (and Uname/Gname) to stable values (commonly 0/0 and empty names) before writing the header.
> 
> On cache hit you only set prevLayerDigest and continue, but you never append the cached layer to currentLayers. Subsequent cache-miss steps will assemble the rootfs without the cached layer, and the final image manifest will omit it. Update currentLayers (and any other build state) the same way as on a cache miss when reusing a cached digest.
> 
> rootfs cleanup is deferred inside the instruction loop; with many steps this accumulates defers and keeps potentially large directories around until the entire build exits. Consider cleaning up at the end of each iteration (e.g., wrap the step in an inner function or call os.RemoveAll explicitly) to reduce disk usage and avoid exhausting /tmp.
> 
> 
> 
> ExtractLayer joins rootfs with header.Name without validating that the resulting path stays within rootfs. A tar entry with an absolute path or ".." segments can write outside the rootfs (path traversal). Sanitize/clean header.Name and reject any path that escapes rootfs before creating files/dirs/symlinks.
> 
> 
> CreateDeltaTar only emits new/modified paths; deletions (e.g., RUN rm) are never represented in the layer, so removed files will reappear when layers are re-extracted. You likely need to detect paths present in beforeState but missing after execution and encode them as whiteouts (and teach ExtractLayer to apply them).
> 
> 


</details>

## ¿Qué hace este PR?
Resuelve el error 500 durante la ingesta de documentos causado por incompatibilidad de versiones entre `qdrant-client` y el servidor Qdrant.

## Causa raíz
`qdrant-client` 1.17.x resolvió en `uv.lock` pero el servidor Docker estaba en `v1.9.0`. La diferencia de versiones menores (8) superaba el límite permitido de 1, causando:
```
UserWarning: Qdrant client version 1.17.1 is incompatible with server version 1.9.0.
vector_store_failed error="Failed to index 588 chunks for 'test_codigo_civil.pdf'"
POST /ingest HTTP/1.1" 500 Internal Server Error
```

## Cambios
- `docker-compose.yml`: `qdrant/qdrant:v1.9.0` → `qdrant/qdrant:v1.13.0`
- `pyproject.toml`: `qdrant-client>=1.12.0` → `qdrant-client>=1.12.0,<1.15.0` (garantiza diff ≤1 con servidor 1.13.x)
- `uv.lock`: regenerado (`qdrant-client` 1.17.0 → 1.14.3)

- [x] Tests unitarios pasan (`360 passed`) — incluidos todos los tests de `QdrantVectorStore`
- [x] Cobertura 98% ≥ 80% verificada
- [x] Lint limpio (`make lint`)

El healthcheck de Qdrant usa `bash -c "cat /dev/null > /dev/tcp/localhost/6333"` (sin curl/wget) — sigue siendo válido en v1.13.0.

Al desplegar, es necesario **recrear el volumen de Qdrant** ya que el formato de almacenamiento puede haber cambiado:
```bash
docker compose down
docker volume rm template_rag_public_exam_qdrant_data  # ajustar nombre del proyecto
```

body:
Greptile Summary

This PR introduces **selective chart tracking** — a significant UX and architecture upgrade for the Monitoring page. The "Alerts" page is renamed to "Monitoring" and gains: real-time consumer group and topic lag ranking tables, interactive multi-entity time-series charts (area/line/bar with up to 5 overlaid entities), and a two-tier recording model where entities are either *persistently tracked* via glob patterns in config or *ephemerally tracked* while present on the chart. The backend gains `SetActiveChartEntities` for ephemeral recording and `matchesAnyGlob` for pattern-based filtering. The frontend gains the `wails-ready` utility to guard against calling Go bindings before the Wails runtime is available. **Key changes:** - New `/monitoring` route replaces `/alerts`, with `MonitoringPage` as the root component housing ranking tables, interactive charts, alert history dialog, and config dialog - `ClusterAlertConfig` extended with `trackedTopics` (opt-in, empty = record nothing) and `trackedGroups` (opt-out, empty = record all for backward compat) - `SetActiveChartEntities` Go method + frontend hook allows ephemeral recording of chart entities not covered by tracked patterns - `Button` and `DialogContent` refactored to `React.forwardRef` for proper ref forwarding - `waitForWails` utility defers Wails Go binding calls until `window.go` is populated **Issues found:** - `frontend/wailsjs/go/models.ts`: Generated model assigns `trackedTopics`/`trackedGroups` directly from `source` without a `?? []` fallback — existing users with stored configs missing these fields will get `undefined` at runtime, bypassing TypeScript's non-optional type guarantees - `lag-charts-tab.tsx`: The reconnect sync effect deliberately disables the exhaustive-deps lint rule, creating a stale closure risk — if entities change while Kafka is disconnected, the reconnect fires with outdated entity data; using refs is the safer pattern here - `monitoring-config-tab.tsx`: `handleAddRule`, `handleUpdateRule`, and `handleDeleteRule` lack `try/catch`, leaving errors silently unhandled and the `saving` state unmanaged on failure - `lag-ranking-tab.tsx` / `lag-monitor-tab.tsx`: `isSuccess`, `isFetching`, and `dataUpdatedAt` are destructured from `useKafkaQuery` but never used

Confidence Score: 3/5

- Functionally solid PR but has a runtime regression risk for existing users via missing null-safe defaults in the generated model file. - The architecture and overall implementation quality are high. However, the missing `?? []` in `models.ts` is a real backwards-compatibility hazard for existing users whose saved configs don't have the new fields — this can cause runtime exceptions without TypeScript warnings. The stale-closure issue in the reconnect effect is a behavioural edge case that may not be immediately visible but can cause silent data-sync failures after a reconnect. body:
## Purpose

This PR adds a tuned fused MoE config for the A100 local EP shape used by HunyuanImage3:

- device: `NVIDIA_A100-SXM4-80GB`
- local shape: `E=16, N=3072`
- dtype: `bf16`

Previously, no tuned config existed for this shape, so the fused MoE kernel fell back to the default Triton configuration.


## Motivation

During investigation of the HunyuanImage3 EP regression (vllm-omni#2015), we found that the local MoE shape:

- `E=16`
- `N=3072`

is exercised under TP=4 + EP on A100, and currently uses the default Triton config.

Profiling indicates that the regression is concentrated in the expert compute path (first Triton expert kernel), suggesting that the default config is suboptimal for this shape.



## Tuned config

The configuration was generated using the official benchmark script on A100 with TP=4:

```bash
python benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe.py \
  --model /path/to/HunyuanImage-3.0 \
  --tp-size 4 \
  --tune \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --save-dir ./configs
```
## Kernel Benchmark Comparison

| Batch Size | Baseline (us) | Tuned (us) | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 842.91 | 843.05 | 1.00x |
| 2 | 1477.72 | 1480.26 | 1.00x |
| 4 | 1968.82 | 2001.55 | 0.98x |
| 8 | 2124.56 | 2126.99 | 1.00x |
| 16 | 2144.33 | 2135.83 | 1.00x |
| 24 | 2163.29 | 2146.95 | 1.01x |
| 32 | 2722.83 | 2155.35 | 1.26x |
| 48 | 2186.90 | 2172.21 | 1.01x |
| 64 | 2769.27 | 2198.24 | 1.26x |
| 96 | 3092.62 | 2211.22 | 1.40x |
| 128 | 2843.98 | 2737.90 | 1.04x |
| 256 | 4189.04 | 3470.30 | 1.21x |
| 512 | 7008.46 | 6230.43 | 1.12x |
| 1024 | 12324.64 | 11708.29 | 1.05x |
| 1536 | 17670.50 | 15051.41 | 1.17x |
| 2048 | 23084.18 | 19780.58 | 1.17x |
| 3072 | 33757.21 | 29335.96 | 1.15x |
| 4096 | 44689.56 | 38574.08 | 1.16x |
| 8192 | 88428.19 | 78207.76 | 1.13x |

Kernel benchmark numbers were obtained with `benchmark_moe.py` by comparing the default fallback path (config file temporarily removed) against the tuned path (config file present) on A100.

author: ziqizhang
body:
## Summary

Add NMF (Non-negative Matrix Factorization) ranker as a new unsupervised ATERanker. Part of #92 (P2.3).

### How it works

1. Build document-candidate frequency matrix (raw counts) from existing JATE candidates
2. Decompose with NMF: A ≈ WH (sklearn, Frobenius norm)
3. Extract top-T candidates per topic from topic-candidate matrix H
4. Union across topics, score = max coefficient
5. Return ranked TermExtractionResult

Based on Section 3.1 of Nugumanova et al. (2024), "Semantic Non-Negative Matrix Factorization for Term Extraction". The base NMF method was evaluated on ACTER (TermEval 2020) and reported as second only to supervised methods.

### Usage

```python
# Via API
result = jate.extract_corpus(docs, algorithm="nmf")

# Via CLI
jate corpus path/to/docs/ --algorithm nmf

# Custom parameters
from jate.algorithms.nmf import NMFRanker
ranker = NMFRanker(n_topics=10, top_n_per_topic=30)
```

### Parameters

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| `n_topics` | 20 | Number of latent topics (k) |
| `top_n_per_topic` | 50 | Top candidates per topic (T). None = score all. |

### Properties

- Unsupervised — no training data needed
- CPU-only — no GPU required
- Lightweight — uses scikit-learn (added as core dependency)
- 13 tests with real data (acl_rdtec_mini)

## Test plan

- [ ] `make check` passes (345 tests + mypy clean)
- [ ] `jate corpus path/ --algorithm nmf` works
- [ ] Different n_topics/top_n_per_topic produce different rankings

author: abh-igyan
body:
## Summary

This PR addresses multiple issues encountered while building Apothesis on Windows using MSYS2/MinGW. The current build instructions are incomplete for Windows environments and lead to configuration and compilation failures.

## Issues Identified

1. CMake Compatibility Issue
   - The project uses an older `cmake_minimum_required` version, which causes errors with newer CMake versions.

2. Missing Toolchain Specification
   - CMake defaults to `NMake Makefiles` on Windows, which requires MSVC.
   - This leads to errors such as:
     - `nmake not found`
     - `CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER not set`

3. Compiler Version Issue
   - The project uses `<any>` (C++17 feature), but older compilers (e.g., GCC 6.3) do not support it.
   - This results in:
     - `fatal error: any: No such file or directory`


Fix Windows build issues and modernize CMake configuration

- Updated cmake_minimum_required to 3.10
- Enforced C++17 standard (required for std::any)
- Added compiler warnings for GCC/Clang
- Improved error handling for unsupported compilers
- Added guidance for Windows (MinGW/MSYS2) builds

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent strategy evaluation and execution on invalid or misaligned market data by enforcing historical data as the source of truth and tightening readiness gating.
- Avoid building full candles from WebSocket ticks, prevent indicators from using the incomplete last candle, and ensure no trading occurs outside market hours.

### Description
- Added `HistoricalLiveOHLCProvider.get_clean_ohlc()` and `is_symbol_valid()` in `src/nifty_scalper_bot/data/source.py` to treat historical API as authoritative and safely overlay only the current live candle without appending duplicates, and to validate OHLC frames for monotonicity, duplicates, NaNs and minimum bars.
- Hardened `StrategyRunner` in `src/nifty_scalper_bot/strategies/runner.py` to: require a configurable minimum number of valid symbols before setting `ready=True`, exclude symbols with invalid data (with logs), validate per-symbol data via `_symbol_has_valid_data()`, and add a periodic historical refresh trigger `_refresh_history_if_due()` to repair drift (default 60s cadence).
- Enforced explicit market session gating in `StrategyRunner._is_market_open()` using IST 09:15–15:30 combined with market state, and added structured logging for market-closed skips.
- Tightened `StrikeSelector.select_contract()` in `src/nifty_scalper_bot/options/strike_selector.py` to attempt resolver refresh if an instrument token is missing and to reject contracts with zero OHLC bars (with logs) before selection.
- Tests: added `tests/data/test_source.py` for `get_clean_ohlc()` and `is_symbol_valid()` behavior and updated `tests/options/test_strike_selector.py` MDM stub to expose `get_ohlc_bars()` used by the selector gate.
- Lightweight, surgical changes only; preserved interfaces and avoided heavy computation in WS pathways.

### Testing
- Ran unit tests: `pytest -q tests/data/test_source.py tests/options/test_strike_selector.py tests/strategies/test_runner_execution_gates.py` — All targeted tests passed (test run succeeded).
- Ran project checks: `bash ./run_checks.sh` — script executed but overall check failed due to pre-existing repository-wide lint/type issues and missing pytest-cov plugin in CI script; these are unrelated to the scoped fixes and were reported in the run output.
- Ran `mypy` against modified files which surfaced broader, pre-existing typing errors across the repository; the typed safety of the incremental changes is preserved but full repo typing cleanup is out-of-scope for this patch.

author: vctrlima
body:
This pull request updates several Grafana dashboard metrics to use more consistent and accurate Prometheus queries, primarily by switching from business-level and DB-specific metrics to HTTP server request metrics with appropriate filters. These changes aim to provide more reliable and unified monitoring across different aspects of the auto repair shop application.

**Dashboard metrics improvements and standardization:**

* Switched work order creation and completion metrics to use sums of HTTP POST and PATCH requests filtered by route and status, instead of business-level counters (`auto_repair_shop_business_work_order_created_total` and `auto_repair_shop_business_work_order_completed_total`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-250383253772ffbf7acb080d0fff76fc114a3729f374dcf5e8caf2c15c0b2143L27-R27) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-250383253772ffbf7acb080d0fff76fc114a3729f374dcf5e8caf2c15c0b2143L46-R46) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-250383253772ffbf7acb080d0fff76fc114a3729f374dcf5e8caf2c15c0b2143L270-R275)
* Updated DB error and authentication failure metrics to use HTTP server request counts filtered by status codes (5xx for errors, 401/403 for auth failures), replacing DB query and business auth failure counters. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-250383253772ffbf7acb080d0fff76fc114a3729f374dcf5e8caf2c15c0b2143L113-R113) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-250383253772ffbf7acb080d0fff76fc114a3729f374dcf5e8caf2c15c0b2143L156-R156) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-250383253772ffbf7acb080d0fff76fc114a3729f374dcf5e8caf2c15c0b2143L293-R303)
* Changed customer creation metric to use a sum of HTTP POST requests to the customer API with 2xx status codes, instead of a business-level customer created counter.
* Modified "in progress" and "completed" work order metrics to use sums of HTTP requests filtered by status codes over the last 24 hours, instead of subtracting business-level counters.

**Query consistency and field renaming:**

* Updated histogram quantile and average duration queries to use the `http_route` label instead of `route`, and to support both `_milliseconds` and non-milliseconds bucket names, improving compatibility and accuracy. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-250383253772ffbf7acb080d0fff76fc114a3729f374dcf5e8caf2c15c0b2143L65-R75) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-250383253772ffbf7acb080d0fff76fc114a3729f374dcf5e8caf2c15c0b2143L132-R137) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-250383253772ffbf7acb080d0fff76fc114a3729f374dcf5e8caf2c15c0b2143L244-R254)
* Standardized HTTP 5xx error queries to consistently use the `http_status_code` label.

**Monitoring coverage expansion:**

* Broadened the "Status" panel to monitor both `otel-collector` and `auto-repair-shop` jobs using a regex match, instead of only the API job.

author: garyjones
body:
## Summary

When a filter callback uses `exit`, `die`, or `throw` instead of returning a value, the `AlwaysReturnInFilter` sniff previously flagged it with the `MissingReturnStatement` error code. While technically correct — the function doesn't return a value to the filter chain — this is misleading in practice. Developers who use `exit` or `throw` in a filter callback have made a deliberate choice to terminate execution; they haven't accidentally forgotten a `return`.

The canonical example is a redirect filter that either returns the URL or calls `wp_redirect()` followed by `exit`. The current sniff treats this identically to a callback that simply forgot to return, which makes the error message unhelpful and forces developers to suppress a generic code that might mask genuine issues elsewhere.

This PR introduces a `hasTerminatingStatement()` check that scans the function body for `T_EXIT` (covering both `exit` and `die`) and `T_THROW` tokens. When the sniff finds no unconditional return but does find a terminating statement, it now emits a `TerminatingInsteadOfReturn` **warning** with a specific message, rather than the generic `MissingReturnStatement` **error**. Callbacks with genuinely missing returns (no terminating statements either) continue to receive the original error.

This gives users a distinct, suppressible code (`WordPressVIPMinimum.Hooks.AlwaysReturnInFilter.TerminatingInsteadOfReturn`) for cases where the pattern is intentional, without silently ignoring potentially problematic code.

Refs #719.

## Test plan

- [ ] `composer test` passes
- [ ] Filter callbacks with `exit`/`die`/`throw` receive the `TerminatingInsteadOfReturn` warning (not error)
- [ ] Filter callbacks with no return and no terminating statement still receive the `MissingReturnStatement` error
- [ ] Existing test cases remain unaffected

author: copilot
body:
Implements `claw-mail-cal-cli login <account-name>` using Entra ID device code flow, storing `AuthenticationRecord` in Azure Key Vault for silent re-authentication on subsequent runs.

## Description

### New Services & Abstractions
- **`IDeviceCodeCredentialProvider`** — wraps `DeviceCodeCredential.AuthenticateAsync` behind an interface so it can be mocked in unit tests (since `DeviceCodeCredential` is sealed)
- **`IAuthenticationService` / `AuthenticationService`** — orchestrates device code flow; checks Key Vault for a cached `AuthenticationRecord` (`auth-record-{name}`), skips interactive prompt if found, serializes/stores it after first auth; gracefully handles corrupted cached records with a user-friendly warning
- **`IAccountService` / `AccountService`** — persists `Account` records as JSON in Key Vault under `account-{name}`; provides the account type needed to pick the correct tenant ID
- **`IKeyVaultService` / `KeyVaultService`** — thin `SecretClient` wrapper with 404-safe `GetSecretAsync`
- **`KeyVaultNameValidator`** — shared `[GeneratedRegex]`-backed validator that enforces Azure Key Vault secret naming rules (`[a-zA-Z0-9-]+`) used by both `AccountService` and `AuthenticationService`

### New Command
- **`LoginCommand`** — `AsyncCommand<Settings>` with `<account-name>` positional arg; delegates entirely to `IAuthenticationService`
- Personal accounts → `TenantId = "common"`, work accounts → configured `workTenantId`
- Device code prompt displayed via `AnsiConsole.MarkupLine`

### Infrastructure
- **`TypeRegistrar` / `TypeResolver`** — `TypeResolver` is a nested private class inside `TypeRegistrar` (one top-level class per file); bridges `IServiceCollection` with Spectre.Console.Cli DI model
- **`Program.cs`** — uses `CommandApp<DefaultCommand>(registrar)` to preserve the default command behaviour while also registering `login` as a named subcommand; validates `keyVault:vaultUri` is a non-empty absolute URI before constructing `SecretClient`, emitting a clear `InvalidOperationException` message if misconfigured
- **`appsettings.json`** documents required config keys with placeholder values; no secrets hardcoded

### Configuration Shape
```json
{
  "keyVault":  { "vaultUri": "<set-in-user-secrets-or-environment>" },
  "entra": {
    "clientId": "<set-in-user-secrets-or-environment>",
    "personalTenantId": "common",
    "workTenantId": "<set-in-user-secrets-or-environment>"
  }
}
```

💡 What: Refactored `parseIdFromUrl` to use a reverse `for` loop and `parseInt()` natively, instead of `.split()`, `.filter()`, and `.map()`.
🎯 Why: `parseIdFromUrl` is called extensively when scraping any CSFD page to extract IDs from lists of related movies, user profiles, or pagination blocks. The previous implementation generated numerous intermediate arrays and ran expensive regex searches on every URL part, causing massive GC overhead and slower execution inside tight parsing loops.
📊 Impact: Expected to reduce CPU time overhead for ID parsing significantly per scrape operation (approx. 5x faster in raw JS micro-benchmarks). Less garbage collection pressure on the JS engine.

author: jonathonbyrdziak
body:
## Summary

- **Nightly builds were using stale cached artifacts** instead of rebuilding after pulling new code
- `INSTALL_REF` was always `"main"` for nightly, so `build-ref == INSTALL_REF` always matched → build skipped
- `yarn install` was skipped if `node_modules/` existed from a previous run, even though dependencies may have changed

## Fixes

- Resolve `INSTALL_REF` to `main@<short-sha>` after checkout so the build cache detects when code actually changed
- Force `yarn install` on nightly — never trust cached `node_modules`
- Don't skip build on nightly when `build-ref` file is missing

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `bash install.sh --nightly` twice — second run should re-install and rebuild (not skip)
- [ ] Run `bash install.sh` (release mode) twice — second run should skip (cached)
- [ ] Verify `dist/.build-ref` contains `main@abc1234` format after nightly build

body:
## Summary

Fixes ProverCoderAI/docker-git#176

Automatically embeds docker-git scripts (session-backup, pre-commit/pre-push guards, knowledge splitter) inside generated Docker containers so that:

- Git hooks referencing `scripts/session-backup-gist.js` work correctly inside containers
- The `setup-pre-commit-hook.js`, `pre-commit-secret-guard.sh`, `pre-push-knowledge-guard.js`, and `split-knowledge-large-files.js` are available for repos cloned inside containers
- Docker-git modules can be used inside the container without manual script copying

## Changes

- **`packages/lib/src/core/templates/dockerfile.ts`**: Added `COPY scripts/ /opt/docker-git/scripts/` layer to embed scripts in Docker image
- **`packages/lib/src/core/templates-entrypoint/tasks.ts`**: After successful clone, symlink `/opt/docker-git/scripts` → `$TARGET_DIR/scripts` so relative paths in hooks resolve
- **`packages/lib/src/core/templates-entrypoint/git.ts`**: Pre-push hook resolves `session-backup-gist.js` from embedded `/opt/docker-git/scripts/` first, with fallback to repo-local `scripts/`
- **`packages/lib/src/shell/files.ts`**: Added `provisionDockerGitScripts()` — copies scripts from workspace into project build context on create/update
- **`packages/lib/src/core/docker-git-scripts.ts`**: New module defining `dockerGitScriptNames` — inventory of scripts to embed
- **`packages/lib/src/core/templates.ts`**: Added `scripts/` to `.gitignore` template (provisioned scripts are derived, not source)

### Инварианты:
- `∀ script ∈ dockerGitScriptNames: accessible(/opt/docker-git/scripts/{script})`

body:
## Summary

- Adds `--json` / `-j` flag for machine-readable JSON output in both list and single-session modes. Agents can parse this programmatically for monitoring other agents.
- Adds `--status` / `-s` flag that fetches the session status endpoint alongside the screen, showing state, uptime, bytes read/written, and WebSocket client count as a header.
- Adds `--watch` / `-w` flag for auto-refreshing screen output with configurable `--interval` / `-n` (default 2s). Clears terminal and re-fetches on each tick. Exits cleanly on Ctrl+C.

### Example usage

```bash
# Agent-optimized: get structured JSON for all sessions
coop peek --json

# Agent-optimized: get screen + status as JSON for one session
coop peek <session-id> --json

# Human: watch a session with status header
coop peek <session-id> --status --watch

# Human: watch with custom interval
coop peek <session-id> --watch --interval 5
```

### JSON output format (single session)
```json
{
  "session_id": "...",
  "screen": { "lines": [...], "ansi": [...], "cols": 120, "rows": 40 },
  "status": { "state": "working", "uptime_secs": 8100, "bytes_read": 1234567, ... }
}
```

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo check -p coop` passes (CI)
- [ ] `coop peek --json` outputs valid JSON array of sessions
- [ ] `coop peek <id> --json` outputs combined screen+status JSON
- [ ] `coop peek <id> --status` shows header line before screen
- [ ] `coop peek <id> --watch` refreshes screen every 2s, exits on Ctrl+C
- [ ] `coop peek <id> --watch --interval 5` uses 5s interval

author: ajitpratap0
body:
## Summary

This PR adds reliability and correctness fixes to the order execution and metrics subsystems.

### Changes

- **WithTx retry safety**: Reset order struct fields (`ID`, `Status`, `ExecutedQuantity`, `ExecutedQuoteQuantity`, `FilledAt`, `AveragePrice`, `UpdatedAt`) before each retry attempt in `WithTx` to prevent stale data from a failed attempt leaking into subsequent retries. UUID is regenerated on each attempt to prevent PK collisions with rolled-back rows.
- **Shutdown reliability**: Improved graceful shutdown — `metricsUpdater.Stop()` is now deferred immediately after `StartAsync` so it always runs on exit. `log.Fatal → log.Error + os.Exit(1)` ensures deferred cleanup runs before process exit, with non-zero exit code so K8s/Docker still detect failures.
- **Metrics lifecycle fixes**:
  - `Stop()` is idempotent via `sync.Once` (already existed).
  - `StartAsync()` is now also idempotent via `sync.Once` — repeated calls no longer launch extra goroutines.
  - `StartAsync + wg.Wait()` in `Stop()` ensures no DB queries race with pool teardown.
- **Sharpe ratio correctness**: Bessel's correction (n-1 denominator for sample variance) + guard for fewer than 2 data points. Added `rows.Err()` check after scan loop to catch mid-stream network errors.
- **MCP panic recovery**: Added `panicRecoveryMiddleware` in `internal/mcp/transport.go` so unhandled panics in MCP handlers return a 500 instead of crashing the server. Includes `r.URL.Path` in the error log for easier correlation.

### Note on MCP server MetricsPort

The opt-in metrics port change for `cmd/mcp-servers/` (`--metrics-port` flag, default disabled) is in **PR #108**, not this PR.

### Note on auth fix

The commit `8fabac54` (_"fix(security): apply AuthMiddleware to /config, /sessions, /positions, /agents endpoints"_) was already merged to `main` before this branch was cut — `routes.go` is not changed here.

### Testing

- `go build ./...` passes
- `go vet ./...` passes
- `gofmt -l .` reports no formatting issues

author: plbrault
body:
## Summary
Major refactoring of Process and IoQueue to implement a proper state machine architecture. Processes now explicitly track their state through a `ProcessState` enum, with state transitions managed through a centralized `apply_state_transition()` method.

## Key Changes

### Process State Machine
- Added `ProcessState` enum with 8 states:
  - `IDLE` - Process not using CPU
  - `RUNNING` - Process actively using CPU
  - `BLOCKED_ON_CPU_IO_REQUESTED` - Blocked for I/O while on CPU
  - `BLOCKED_ON_CPU_IO_AVAILABLE` - I/O arrived but not yet delivered
  - `BLOCKED_ON_CPU_PAGE_FAULT` - Blocked waiting for page swap
  - `BLOCKED_OFF_CPU_IO_REQUESTED` - Blocked for I/O off CPU
  - `BLOCKED_OFF_CPU_IO_AVAILABLE` - I/O arrived off CPU
  - `ENDED` - Process terminated

- Added `StateEvent` enum representing events that trigger state transitions:
  - `ASSIGN_TO_CPU`, `REMOVE_FROM_CPU`
  - `REQUEST_IO`, `IO_AVAILABLE`, `IO_DELIVERED`
  - `PAGE_FAULT`, `PAGE_AVAILABLE`
  - `TERMINATE_GRACEFULLY`, `TERMINATE_FROM_STARVATION`

### Architecture Improvements
- **Centralized state transitions**: All state changes go through `apply_state_transition()`
- **Removed convenience properties**: `is_running`, `has_ended`, `is_waiting_for_page`, `io_event_arrived` - replaced with direct state checks
- **Consolidated timing**: `_last_state_change_time` is now updated only in `apply_state_transition()`
- **Refactored event handling**: Renamed `events` to `player_actions` for clarity

### IoQueue Changes
- Renamed `process_events()` to `handle_player_action()` - clearer intent
- Added space key support for delivering I/O events

### Behavior Changes
1. **Starvation suspended**: Process starvation no longer increases while in `BLOCKED_*_IO_REQUESTED` states
2. **Starvation resumes**: Once I/O event arrives (`*_IO_AVAILABLE`), starvation increases again
3. **Starvation resets**: When I/O is delivered (`IO_DELIVERED`), starvation resets to 0
4. **Removed restriction**: Processes can now request I/O even at `LAST_ALIVE_STARVATION_LEVEL`

### Code Quality
- All code passes pylint (10.00/10)
- Added comprehensive test coverage for state transitions
- Refactored private methods for clarity
- Added specs documentation (`specs/process_state_machine.md`)

## Testing
- Added `TestStateEvents` test class with 23 tests covering all valid and invalid state transitions
- Updated existing tests to use state-based assertions
- Added spy fixture to verify `apply_state_transition()` is called with correct events
- All 243 tests passing

author: fwbrasil
body:
## Problem

JCTools is one of the remaining dependencies in Kyo's base modules and is available only for the JVM. We currently have unoptimized stubs in Native due to this limitation. The performance of `TracePool` in Native is quite bad due to the performance of the stubs.

## Solution

Port the JCTools queues. I've decided to try to keep the code as close as possible to the original given the complexity of memory ordering in the implementations. For example, I tried to use `Maybe` but got quite odd inconsistencies. 

## Notes

- I've decided to keep the implementations in `kyo-data` so it's available to internal code in the base modules. It's used by `TracePool` in `kyo-kernel` and `Queue` in `kyo-core`.
- I tried the new impl in the scheduler but the current worker queue is better optimized for the specific use case.
- Although I kept the internal logic not using Kyo's safe primitives, all APIs return the expected Kyo type. For example, a `Maybe` where the API can return `null`.
- I've moved `AllowUnsafe` to `kyo-data` so we can use it to properly mark the APIs as unsafe.

body:
## Summary

Adds [Model Context Protocol](https://spec.modelcontextprotocol.io) (MCP) as a new UI server transport type, enabling LLM agents and AI tools to control the simulator programmatically. Deprecates the HTTP transport in favor of MCP.

## Changes

### New: `ApplicationProtocol.MCP` transport type
- `UIMCPServer extends AbstractUIServer` — MCP server on `/mcp` endpoint using `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` v1.27.1
- Stateless `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` (JSON-RPC 2.0)
- Promise bridge: `pendingMcpRequests` map bridges async broadcast channel responses to MCP tool handlers
- Security: rate limiting, body size limit, 404 for non-/mcp paths, 400 for malformed JSON

### MCP Tools (all 33 `ProcedureName` entries)
All UI procedures exposed as MCP tools with version-aware OCPP payload schemas:
- 16 OCPP command tools with `ocpp16Payload` / `ocpp20Payload` optional fields
- Full OCPP JSON Schemas injected at runtime from existing `src/assets/json-schemas/ocpp/` files (no duplication)
- Pre-flight version compatibility check with clear error messages per station
- Mutual exclusivity validation (cannot provide both payload versions)
- Version affinity annotations in tool descriptions: `(OCPP 1.6 only)`, `(OCPP 2.0.x only)`, `(OCPP 1.6 & 2.0.x)`
- 15 version-agnostic tools (station control, simulator control) unchanged
- 2 log read tools (`readCombinedLog`, `readErrorLog`) with `tail` parameter (default 200, max 5000)

### MCP Resources (read-only)
- `station://list` — All charging stations with status
- `station://{hashId}` — Individual station data
- `template://list` — Available configuration templates
- `schema://ocpp/{version}` — List available OCPP command schemas per version
- `schema://ocpp/{version}/{command}` — Full OCPP JSON Schema for a specific command

### Deprecated: `UIHttpServer`
- `@deprecated` JSDoc on class and `start()` method
- Runtime deprecation warning logged when HTTP transport is used
- Factory updated with `// eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-deprecated`

### Code quality
- `HttpMethod` enum extracted to shared `UIServerUtils.ts` (replaces string literals across all transports)
- `BaseError` used instead of generic `Error`
- DRY: `createToolErrorResponse()`/`createToolResponse()` helpers, `closeTransportSafely()`, `registerLogReadTool()` factory

- Log messages harmonized with existing transport patterns

author: mattemusacchio
body:
Fixes #2132

## Problem
GSD auto-mode hangs when executing tasks that run long-running commands like npm run dev or npm test because the agent uses synchronous bash tool instead of asynchronous alternatives.

## Root Cause
The execute-task prompt template did not provide clear guidelines for tool selection:
- No instruction to use async_bash for commands expected to complete but take >10s
- No guidance to use bg_shell for indefinite processes like dev servers
- Agents default to bash for all commands, causing hangs on test suites or builds

## Solution
Added a Tool Selection Guidelines section that instructs agents to:
- Use bash for commands completing in <10 seconds (file operations, quick builds, single commands)
- Use async_bash + await_job for commands taking 10s+ that complete (tests, builds, installs)
- Use bg_shell for indefinite processes (dev servers, watchers, daemons)
- Never use bash with & - it causes hangs due to stream inheritance

## Testing
The guidelines are already in use by the GSD auto-mode executor and have been validated to prevent hangs on long-running commands.
